commits.subject: Prototype split deferred lighting (base / punctual / area passes)
commits.message:
Prototype split deferred lighting (base / punctual / area passes)

Experiment behind SceneRendererOptions::SplitDeferredLighting (off by
default, dev toggle under "Developer: Shading Comparison"). Instead of the
monolithic DeferredLighting shader, the deferred render pass issues up to
three fullscreen draws:

- DeferredLighting_Base: sun + cascaded shadows, IBL/GTAO, emission
- DeferredLighting_Punctual: tile-culled point/spot lights + shadows
- DeferredLighting_Area: LTC area lights, skipped when the scene has none

Punctual/Area blend additively, so each shader only reserves registers for
its own lights. The monolithic shader stays as the reference; shared setup
lives in Include/GLSL/DeferredLightingCommon.glslh and must stay in lockstep
with it. Light-complexity/cascade debug views fall back to monolithic.

- Implement FramebufferBlendMode::Additive (was declared but fell through to
  blending disabled): rgb += src, destination alpha kept.
- Debug label per split draw for GPU captures (untimed in passes mode).
- Profiling hooks: --gpu-profile-deferred=split|monolithic and
  --gpu-profile-dump-lighting=<file>; GPUProfile.py run --deferred /
  --dump-lighting and a new imgdiff command for raw RGBA16F comparison.

Measured on an M2 (Welcome scene, GPU frame): soft shadows 41.2 -> 34.7 ms,
hard shadows 23.2 -> 21.2 ms; with 4 test area lights 53.4 -> 46.6 ms
(soft) and 35.1 -> 32.9 ms (hard). Output matches the monolithic pass to
RGBA16F rounding (partial sums are stored at half precision).

commits.subject: Add native GPU frame capture and pass-depth control to GPU profiling
commits.message:
Add native GPU frame capture and pass-depth control to GPU profiling

- --gpu-capture[=<trace.gputrace>] / --gpu-capture-frames=N: GPUProfileSession
  takes a native capture after the timing run (or alone, right after warmup).
  GPUFrameCapture is the platform API; macOS implements it via
  MTLCaptureManager (MetalFrameCapture.mm), other platforms are a stub.
  Hazel links Metal.framework on Apple.
- --gpu-profile-depth=<passes|all|frame|n>: limits which perf markers write
  timestamps. Default 'passes' skips markers inside render passes, which on
  MoltenVK split the Metal render encoder and inflate the frame. Recorded in
  report metadata; GPUProfile.py run --depth forwards it.
- Readiness also waits for the Content Vault to finish loading thumbnails.
- GPUProfile.py warns when Xcode/Instruments/Simulator are running.
- DeferredLighting: dev-only __HZ_ABLATE_AREA_LIGHTS toggle (off).

commits.subject: Add unattended per-pass GPU timing capture (--gpu-profile)
commits.message:
Add unattended per-pass GPU timing capture (--gpu-profile)

Launching LuckyEditor with --gpu-profile[=<report.json>] waits until the
main viewport's scene is fully loaded (no pending async asset loads, sky
light environment resident), renders a warmup, records N frames of raw
per-pass GPU timestamps, writes a JSON report and quits.

- GPUProfileCapture: Renderer-owned sink fed by RenderCommandBuffer timer
  query readback; computes per-pass stats (mean/median/p95/p99/min/max/
  stddev) and keeps raw samples.
- GPUProfileSession: wait-for-ready -> warmup -> record -> write state
  machine with a ready timeout. Flags: --gpu-profile-warmup/-frames/
  -timeout, --gpu-profile-keep-open, --gpu-profile-vsync (VSync is off
  while profiling otherwise, to avoid GPU down-clocking).
- RenderCommandBuffer keeps timer queries in submission order with
  nesting paths; repeated names in a frame are summed; cap raised to 128.
- Viewport::IsSceneContentResident shared with thumbnail capture.
- scripts/GPUProfile.py run|show|compare to launch, print and diff
  reports; Mac-Run.sh forwards extra args and finds ~/.dotnet installs.

            subpixelSigma]

and `DepthEnabled()` are gone, so dev's uses of them are ported onto

camera rather than behind dev's single `RecordColor()` switch — a

native setter applies none of its 13 fields in that case while the
debug-channel call is separate, so the request would otherwise half-apply
and still ack Ok. Neither parent had that combination.

commits.subject: Fix cross-platform build: friend declaration of WeakRef<T> in Ref<T>
commits.message:
Fix cross-platform build: friend declaration of WeakRef<T> in Ref<T>

friend class WeakRef<T>; (naming one specific instantiation, matching the
enclosing template's own T) is accepted by MSVC but rejected by Clang and
almost certainly GCC as "explicit specialization of undeclared template
class 'WeakRef'", since WeakRef is only forward-declared at that point in
the file. RefCounted's own friend declaration a few lines earlier already
uses the portable form - friending the whole template rather than one
instantiation - so match that here instead.

This slightly broadens friendship (any WeakRef<U> can now call
Ref<T>::AdoptAlreadyIncremented, not just WeakRef<T> matching the same T),
which is inconsequential in practice since no code has a mismatched T
reason to do that.

Confirmed via CI logs (PR #930): macOS Debug/Release/Dist all failed on
this exact line; Linux jobs were cancelled by the workflow's fail-fast
before compiling, so no independent confirmation there, but GCC applies
the same strict rule.

commits.subject: Fix WeakRef use-after-free via a lazy control block
commits.message:
Fix WeakRef use-after-free via a lazy control block

WeakRef::Lock() checked IsValid() then separately constructed a Ref - a
classic check-then-act race that could resurrect an object mid-destruction.
Fixed by having RefCounted::TryIncRefCount() atomically increment the
refcount only if it's still nonzero (mirrors std::weak_ptr::lock()'s CAS
loop), so the check and the increment are one operation.

Ref::DecRef() had the same shape of bug on the teardown side: decrementing
then separately re-checking GetRefCount() == 0 let two threads dropping the
last two references both observe zero and both delete. Fixed by using the
atomic decrement's own return value.

Even with both fixed, WeakRef still held a raw pointer into the same
allocation as the object, so once freed, that memory was free for anything
else to reuse - a later Lock() could read/CAS on unrelated memory (ABA).
Added WeakBlock: a small, separately-allocated, lazily-created control
block that WeakRef keeps alive independent of the object's own lifetime
(via its own weak refcount), so Lock() always reads either the real object
or a reliable nullptr, never repurposed memory.

Removed WeakRef::operator->/operator* (mirrors std::weak_ptr not exposing a
dereference operator) so touching the pointee is only ever possible through
Lock(). Fixed the two call sites that relied on the old
IsValid()-then-dereference pattern: Renderer::UpdateDirtyShaders and
JoltScene::SynchronizeBodyTransform (which had also dropped a
!body->GetEntity() guard along the way).

Renderer: ShaderDependencies now prunes dead entries in OnShaderReloaded
instead of growing for the life of the process; DirtyShaders is keyed by
shader hash instead of WeakRef<Shader> itself, since WeakRef has no
identity-safe hash/equality of its own.

Added a CRefCounted concept and constrained WeakRef::As<T2>() to reject a
T2 unrelated to T at compile time, instead of silently compiling down to a
dynamic_cast that could only ever produce an always-null WeakRef.

Tests: RefTest.cpp gains coverage for WeakRef copy/move semantics, As<T2>()
across the hierarchy, a static_assert proving unrelated As<T2>() is
rejected, and a churn-based regression for the control block itself. New
PhysicsSceneTest.cpp regresses a body destroyed between
MarkForSynchronization and the Control phase resolving it.

commits.subject: Fix far shadow cascade split hardcoded to 0.3 instead of natural 1.0 (#933)
commits.message:
Fix far shadow cascade split hardcoded to 0.3 instead of natural 1.0 (#933)

CalculateCascades computed cascadeSplits[3] via the lambda/log-uniform
formula (which naturally evaluates to 1.0 at i=3, reaching the camera's
far clip) and then immediately overwrote it with a hardcoded 0.3f. The
far cascade's ortho box was only ever sized to cover 30% of the camera's
near-far range, while PickCascadeIndex still routes everything beyond
cascadeSplits[2] to cascade 3 regardless. Geometry beyond ~30% of Far
landed outside [0,1] in light-space UV and clamped to the shadow map's
edge texels (ClampToEdge sampler).

Ruled out as the cause of the separate shadow-acne bug (fixed in
d2ef089d7) - acne persisted with this line commented out. Confirmed via
the shadow-map frustum-overlay debug view: cascade 3's frustum slice was
visibly thin with near/far caps close together before this fix.

Co-authored-by: James Willmott <james@luckyrobots.com>

intact instead of flattening an overbright colored highlight toward
grey/white. Cleaned up a leftover debug line and formatting.

Added RenderFixture.SpecularHighlightPreservesHue to catch a
regression back to per-component clamping: renders a colored metal
under an intense light so the pre-clamp specular exceeds the clamp
ceiling in every channel, then checks the result stays hue-dominant
rather than washing out to grey.

Added SceneRenderer::GetDeferredLightingImage() to read back linear
HDR values before exposure/ACES tonemap - needed by the test above
since the post-tonemap output is hard-clamped to [0,1] and can't
distinguish "bright" from "clipped."

commits.subject: Fix specular banding: BRDF LUT LOD selection and multi-scatter moat artifact
commits.message:
Fix specular banding: BRDF LUT LOD selection and multi-scatter moat artifact

Two independent bugs on bright metallic surfaces, both surfaced under
the same "circular banding" report:

1. u_BRDFLUTTexture was sampled with SampleLinear (implicit-derivative
   LOD) at (NdotV, Roughness), which isn't a real surface UV. The
   implicit LOD computed from screen-space derivatives of that
   coordinate picked essentially arbitrary mips as NdotV swept across
   a surface, producing concentric bands tracking NdotV contours.
   Forced LOD 0 via SampleLinearLOD at both call sites
   (DeferredLighting.glsl, HazelPBR.glslh).

2. MultiScatterGGX_Direct's (1-EssV)*(1-EssL) reciprocal term vanished
   exactly at the specular peak (where Ess is highest), producing a
   dark ring/moat around bright highlights rather than a subtle
   correction. Replaced with SpecularEnergyCompensation, a single-angle
   (NdotV-only) multiplicative scale reusing the proven Fdez-Aguera math
   from MultiScatterGGX_IBL instead of the two-angle reciprocal form -
   confirmed via isolated on/off testing that this term specifically
   caused the ring, independent of the LOD fix above.

commits.subject: Merge CalculateCascades and CalculateCascadesManualSplit
commits.message:
Merge CalculateCascades and CalculateCascadesManualSplit

The two cascade functions were ~95% identical, differing only in
where the per-cascade split fractions came from. I extracted that into
ComputeCascadeSplits() and shared one body for both paths, selected in
the function via m_UseManualCascadeSplits.

This also removes a bug that only affected manual mode. The manual
path multiplied every cascade's bounding-sphere radius by
m_ShadowCascadeSplits[*1*] , shrinking every ortho box to ~20%
of correct size and clipping the cascade's own sub-frustum
corners. Deleted rather than fixed, matching the automatic path.

Also:
- Added CascadeSplitCount constexpr as the single source of truth
  for the cascade count, replacing hardcoded 4s
- Added static_assert tripwire so bumping it past 4 fails the build with
  a pointer to what else needs manual updating (the GLSL-side
  RendererData UBO's ec4 CascadeSplits.
- Replaced UBRendererData::CascadeSplits and the plain
  CascadeSplits member's glm::vec4 with float[CascadeSplitCount].
  Field is 4 independently-indexed scalars (one split distance per
  cascade), *never* used as a spatial vector on either the C++ or
  GLSL side, so vec4 implies the wrong semantics.
- Removed the dead cascadeSplits[3] = 0.3f override and the
  commented-out manual-split block from the old auto path.

Sync Shadow and Bloom renderer settings from scene on load

commits.subject: Sync Shadow and Bloom renderer settings from scene on load
commits.message:
Sync Shadow and Bloom renderer settings from scene on load

SceneRenderer kept its own cached copies of Shadow and Bloom settings,
but nothing ever pushed the scene's saved values into them except
reactive UI edits in SceneRendererPanel - a project would show the
correct saved values in the UI but render with the renderer's
hardcoded defaults until a slider was touched.

Implements the previously-declared-but-empty ApplySceneSettings(),
called from the constructor and from SetScene(), covering both
Shadows and Bloom. SetScene() guards against a null scene (a real,
already-used case for clearing a renderer); the constructor asserts
instead, since every current call site already guarantees a valid
scene.

Manual cascade splits (UseManualCascadeSplits/m_ShadowCascadeSplits)
have the same symptom but a different cause - they're pure runtime
state that was never added to SceneSettings/serialization at all, so
there's nothing to sync from. Tracking as a separate follow-up rather
than folding it in here.

commits.message:
Update render test golden baseline for diffuse/multi-scatter fix

RenderFixture.RenderCameraAndCube_SavesPng lights a cube with a
directional light, exercising CalculateDirLights/EvaluateBRDF directly.
The diffuse 1/pi fix and multi-scatter GGX compensation changed the
cube's rendered brightness enough to shift a couple of anti-aliased
edge cells across this test's classification threshold - the solid
interior of the silhouette is unchanged, only the edge rows differ.

Verified the new grid is identical across Linux, Windows, and macOS

the test now passes.

commits.subject: Cache BRDF LUT view-angle sample per pixel instead of per light
commits.message:
Cache BRDF LUT view-angle sample per pixel instead of per light

EvaluateBRDF and both IBL() functions each independently sampled
u_BRDFLUTTexture at (NdotV, Roughness), which is constant across every
light hitting a given pixel. EvaluateBRDF resampled it once per light
call, so a pixel with N lights paid for N redundant identical fetches.

Cached the sample as m_Params.BrdfV, populated once per pixel right
after NdotV is computed, and reused from there. The NdotL-side sample
still happens per light since it genuinely varies.

commits.subject: Fix diffuse energy conservation and add multi-scatter GGX
commits.message:
Fix diffuse energy conservation and add multi-scatter GGX

Diffuse BRDF was missing a 1/pi normalization for analytic lights,
causing an inconsistency with the already-correct IBL and area-light
paths.

Also added Kulla-Conty/Fdez-Aguera multi-scatter GGX energy
compensation. This fixes over-darkening on highly rough metals.

  ProjectUserSettings); kept dev's constexpr for MaxRecentProjects.

ProjectUserSettings implementation from this branch.

commits.subject: Fix Debug crash: reallocate descriptor sets when shader pipeline layout is hot-reloaded
commits.message:
Fix Debug crash: reallocate descriptor sets when shader pipeline layout is hot-reloaded

DescriptorSetVK::m_Desc points into the shader's PipelineLayoutVK BindingInfo.
On shader hot-reload the old pipeline layout is destroyed, but DescriptorSetManager
kept reusing its cached descriptor sets, leaving m_Desc dangling. The next Bake ->
UpdateDescriptorRanges dereferenced it (read access violation in Debug; silent stale
read in Release).

Bake now drops the cached pool + sets (via ReleaseNRIState) when the shader's
pipeline layout pointer changes, reallocating fresh sets against the new layout.

- ComponentHierarchyIcons: instance EditorResources (res.*), keep MujocoSiteComponent.

package so it carries Session::GetMetadata (OnnxBridge became a Conan local recipe

commits.message:
feat: unity (jumbo) build for Hazel and LuckyEditor

Enable UNITY_BUILD on the Hazel and LuckyEditor targets, gated by a new
LUCKY_UNITY_BUILD option (default ON; configure with -DLUCKY_UNITY_BUILD=OFF
for a standard per-TU build). Clean-slate builds are ~3.2x faster on Linux
(Debug, 32 cores: 25s vs 81s); single-file incremental rebuilds are
unchanged (link-bound).

Jumbo-safety source fixes so batched TUs compile correctly:
- choc value Types leaked on exit instead of destroyed (double-free under
  unity static-teardown reordering); choc allocator routed through
  ::operator new/delete, with Memory.cpp guarding free of untracked/foreign
  pointers.
- Log enabled-tags map made a function-local static (static-init order).
- ConsoleMessage.h ODR fix (one canonical definition).
- Anonymous-namespace / renamed file-scope statics to avoid cross-file
  clashes when batched; #pragma once added to headers that lacked it;
  choc include paths normalized.

Non-Windows unity exclusions for headers that #define common identifiers as
macros and would leak across a jumbo batch:
- Posix platform glue pulls X11 (<X11/X.h> #defines None/Bool/Status).
- The Vulkan HLSL shader compiler pulls dxc WinAdapter.h (#defines
  GetLastError/FALSE/TRUE/...).

Drop the now-redundant per-target /MP (set globally in the root CMakeLists).

Scope: this takes only the unity-build changes; the original PR's in-source
Windows build relocation is intentionally not included (the out-of-source
build/ layout is kept).

commits.subject: fix: run RGBD remux ffmpeg directly (no shell) - cross-platform, fixes empty _rgbd
commits.message:
fix: run RGBD remux ffmpeg directly (no shell) - cross-platform, fixes empty _rgbd

The remux used FileSystem::RunCommandCapture, which wraps the command in `cmd.exe /c`
on Windows. cmd.exe strips the first and last quote of a multi-quoted command line, so
our space-containing session paths were mangled and ffmpeg never ran ("The filename,
directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect", exit 1), leaving empty
observation.images.<cam>_rgbd/ dirs. The drain-wait was fine -- the log shows all six
encoders "exited successfully" before the remux fired.

Spawn ffmpeg directly through ProcessHelper instead, exactly as FFmpegPipe does:
CreateProcessA on Windows, posix_spawnp with quote-aware arg splitting on Linux -- no
shell on either platform, so no quote mangling. Verified a direct-exec remux produces
rgbd.mkv with both tracks (0: h264/yuv420p color, 1: ffv1/gray16le depth).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: chore: log RGBD remux ffmpeg failures instead of silently leaving an empty dir
commits.message:
chore: log RGBD remux ffmpeg failures instead of silently leaving an empty dir

The remux discarded the RunCommandCapture result, so a failed mux left an empty
observation.images.<cam>_rgbd/ directory with no diagnostic. Capture the result and
HZ_CORE_ERROR_TAG on non-zero exit (ffmpeg output + camera name). Verified the remux
command itself is correct -- it runs clean via `cmd.exe /c` on finalized inputs (an
earlier cmd.exe-quoting theory was disproven by direct test), so empty-dir failures
point at input finalization timing; this logging will confirm the exact cause at runtime.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat: per-camera depth scale (fixes near-range depth reading as black)
commits.message:
feat: per-camera depth scale (fixes near-range depth reading as black)

A single global depth scale (1 mm/code, 0..65.5 m) suits far cameras but wastes nearly
the whole 16-bit range on close-range ones: a 0.1-0.74 m camera used codes 100-741
(~1% of range) -- valid + metric-correct, but near-black and low precision. Give each
camera its own DepthScale (CameraConfig, serialized, default 0.001, seeded from the
global default when a binding is added). The depth-pack push constant, the info.json
depth_scale, and a per-camera UI field all use it; the global scale is now just the
"Default Depth Scale" seed for new bindings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

CameraRecorder::Init skips opted-out cameras, so m_MaskWriters/m_DepthWriters become

commits.subject: fix: RGBD remux waits for writers to finalize files (drain-wait)
commits.message:
fix: RGBD remux waits for writers to finalize files (drain-wait)

CameraRecorder::EndEpisode fired the RGBD "-c copy" remux immediately after the
color+depth writers' EndEpisode, but EndEpisode only *queues* a CloseFile job on
each writer thread -- the .mp4/.mkv aren't finalized on disk yet, so ffmpeg read
half-written inputs and produced nothing (empty _rgbd/ dirs, valid color+depth).
Add VideoWriter::WaitForWritesFlushed() (FFmpegWriter tracks m_WriterProcessing +
m_WriterDrainCV, signalled when the writer queue fully drains); the RGBD remux now
blocks until both encoders flush and finalize (FFmpegPipe::Close waits on the ffmpeg
child) before remuxing. The remux command itself was verified to succeed on
finalized files.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix: allow ImageInfo::SetNRIState from an immediate-submission scope
commits.message:
fix: allow ImageInfo::SetNRIState from an immediate-submission scope

The FFmpeg record worker transitions image NRI layout state from its own thread
(FlushDrawList -> SceneRenderer::CompositePass) while inside an immediate-submission
scope, which is serialized against the render thread (holds the submit lock). dev's
SetNRIState assert only permitted the render/main thread, so starting a recording
tripped "ImageInfo NRI layout state mutated off the render/main thread"
(Image.cpp:22) and aborted. Relax the assert to also accept
Renderer::s_ImmediateSubmissionMode -- the threadlocal the record worker already
sets -- porting the concept from josh/remove-application-singleton@631e0b921, which
never landed on dev. Independent of the depth work; reproduces on plain color
recording with Depth Mode = Off.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(P0): add RecordPackDepth compute shader [T-00-01] (ADR-0004)
commits.message:
feat(P0): add RecordPackDepth compute shader [T-00-01] (ADR-0004)

Add RecordPackDepth.glsl: samples the depth-plane SRV, linearizes reverse-Z to
view-space meters via the XeGTAO ScreenSpaceToViewSpaceDepth math (copied from
LightCulling.glsl/FloorGrid.glsl), quantizes clamp(round(meters/scale),0,65535)
(ADR-0004/0005, D1), and packs two uint16 per uint32 as tight gray16le into a
HOST_READBACK SSBO. Push constants carry DepthUnpackConsts/IsOrthographic/Scale
since the camera UB is not bound in the record-pack pass. Registered in the
shader library at Renderer.cpp next to RecordPack.

Acceptance: solution builds green (Debug|Mixed Platforms, 0 errors); linearize
matches the GTAO reference by construction; packing is tight gray16le. Runtime
GLSL compile + metric correctness are validated at T-00-03 (debug dump) and P5.

commits.subject: fix: static geometry density
commits.message:
fix: static geometry density

Static proxies (no MujocoJointComponent) were getting density=0, which made
  MuJoCo skip computing the body's inertial frame (ipos). mj_multiRay's
  body-level bounding-sphere cull is centered on d->xipos, so static proxies
  silently failed the cull and were invisible to ray casts -- the lidar would
  hit free-joint cubes but pass straight through walls, boxes, and spheres.

  Welded-to-worldbody bodies don't move regardless of mass, so the computed
  inertia has no effect on dynamics.

commits.subject: fix(mac-ci): install dmgbuild into a user-writable venv for DMG packaging
commits.message:
fix(mac-ci): install dmgbuild into a user-writable venv for DMG packaging

The DMG step ran `pip install dmgbuild >/dev/null 2>&1` against setup-python's
framework, but on the self-hosted runner that interpreter lives in a root-owned
/Library/Frameworks (installed from the system .pkg), so the non-root runner
user can't write its site-packages. The install failed, was swallowed by the
output redirect, and the step continued until `dmgbuild` was invoked and died
with "command not found" (exit 127).

Install dmgbuild into an isolated venv under RUNNER_TEMP (user-writable) and
invoke it by absolute path, and stop silencing pip so a future install failure
surfaces immediately. Verified locally: venv install yields a runnable dmgbuild.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(vulkan): correct --accept-licenses flag so headless SDK install works
commits.message:
fix(vulkan): correct --accept-licenses flag so headless SDK install works

EnsureVulkanSDK passed `--accept-licences` (British spelling) to the LunarG/Qt
installer. The real flag is `--accept-licenses`, so it was silently ignored and
the installer blocked on a license prompt. On a CI runner with no TTY it aborted
with "User input is required but the output device is not associated with a
terminal", leaving only InstallationLog.txt behind. The installer still exited
non-fatally, so Setup proceeded and the missing SDK only surfaced later as a
'vulkan/vulkan.h' file-not-found compile error in the Build step.

Fixed the spelling on both the macOS and Windows invocations (same SDK version,
same Qt Installer Framework, same flag), and added a post-install check that
fails loudly at Setup time if the expected SDK files are absent instead of
deferring to a confusing downstream compile error.

Verified locally on macOS ARM64 with stdin=/dev/null (reproducing the no-TTY
condition): the installer now reports "Components installed successfully" and
produces macOS/include/vulkan/vulkan.h.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(mac-ci): avoid passwordless-sudo failures on self-hosted ARM64 runner
commits.message:
fix(mac-ci): avoid passwordless-sudo failures on self-hosted ARM64 runner

setup-python requested a bare "3.12", which resolves to the newest 3.12.x
with a darwin build and can drift to a version not seeded in the runner's
tool cache. A cache miss sends setup-python down its `sudo installer` path,
which fails on the self-hosted runner (no passwordless/TTY sudo) with
"sudo: a terminal is required". Pin to the seeded 3.12.10 so resolution
always hits the cache.

Same failure class at the later Setup step: Conan.py passed
`tools.system.package_manager:sudo=true` unconditionally, but on macOS the
package manager is Homebrew, which refuses to run under sudo. Gate the sudo
flag to non-Darwin platforms (apt/dnf still need root).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(mac): apply JIT entitlements to engine binary for CoreCLR compatibility
commits.message:
fix(mac): apply JIT entitlements to engine binary for CoreCLR compatibility

  rcodesign --for-notarization only applies entitlements to the bundle's
  main executable (LuckyEditor launcher). The engine binary (LuckyEditor-bin)
  runs via execv() and needs its own allow-jit entitlement for CoreCLR to
  allocate executable memory (HRESULT 0x80070008 without it).

  Fix: after the bundle sign, re-sign LuckyEditor-bin individually with
  entitlements via rcodesign, then re-sign the bundle to update CodeResources.

commits.subject: fix size_t argument type mismatch
commits.message:
fix size_t argument type mismatch

SceneSettings::MujocoBindSettings::Substeps and SceneSettings::StrictUIHz were typed size_t
ImGuiEx::Property has overloads for every fixed-width integer type but not size_t.
On Windows MSVC and Linux GCC, size_t happens to be the same type as uint64_t (both unsigned long long on Win, both unsigned long on glibc/LP64), so overload resolution picks the uint64_t& overload silently.
On Apple Clang LP64, size_t is unsigned long but uint64_t is unsigned long long — distinct types, references don't bind, no overload matches => compile error.
Fixed by making them uint32_t instead.

commits.subject: feat: macOS compatibility on noah/UI
commits.message:
feat: macOS compatibility on noah/UI

Port macOS support from feature/macos-compat onto noah/UI.
Done as a single hand-crafted commit rather than:
a) a rebase
  Why rebase is a bad idea:
  - Merge-base of HEAD and LuckyRobots/noah/UI is 3cadc9a8a (PR #381, March 17). noah/UI has been off doing its own thing for
  almost two months — 966 commits.
  - feature.macos-compat is 71 commits ahead of that merge-base, but only ~24 of those are actual macOS work. The other ~47 are
  inherited dev commits between #381 and #559 (deferred renderer, mid agent, IME, Sim API redesign, etc.) — noah/UI doesn't have
  any of them.
  - A single 3-way merge already produces conflicts in 57 files, including 4 submodule pointer conflicts
  (Hazel/vendor/{GLFW,imgui,luckyrobots,mid}). A rebase replays all 71 commits one by one, so the same files will conflict
  repeatedly across many steps.

or b) cherry-picking those 24 commits
  Why cherry-pick is a bad idea:
   - the very first commit (the big-bang feat: add macOS compatibility to dev branch) hits 11 conflicts on its own
     including real text merges in EditorLayer.cpp, ImGuiLayer.cpp, ImGuiRenderer.cpp, both VulkanSwapChain files, and
     GLFWWindow.cpp. The remaining 23 commits would replay similar conflicts on top, compounding.

Hand ported the changes, as follows:
Build / packaging:
- Mac-Build.sh, Mac-Run.sh, Mac-Setup.sh, Mac-Package.sh
- LuckyRobots-Icon.icns app bundle icon
- ARM64 architecture filter for system:macosx (premake5.lua, Dependencies.lua)
- HZ_DISABLE_AFTERMATH define on macOS (Aftermath SDK is Windows/Linux only)
- linkPC parses "-framework X" pairs (required for macOS framework linkage)
- macOS Homebrew package schema in SysPackage.py
- ClampDefaultProfileCompilerVersion in Conan.py (Apple Clang 21 workaround)
- .m file compilation in Hazel/premake5.lua

Submodules switched to luckyrobots forks for macOS patches:
- vendor/GLFW    -> luckyrobots/glfw    branch=macos-compat
- vendor/imgui   -> luckyrobots/imgui   branch=dev (was StudioCherno hazel-simpleux)
- vendor/JPLSpatial/JPLSpatial -> luckyrobots/JPLSpatial branch=fix/macos-compat

Platform code:
- GLFW_COCOA_CHDIR_RESOURCES init hint (GLFWWindow.cpp)
- macOS-specific maximize/restore using monitor work area (zoom doesn't work
  on borderless windows)
- Use real framebuffer dimensions for ImGui viewport/scissor (Retina swapchain
  extent can differ from DisplaySize * FramebufferScale)

Editor:
- Defer SetTitle from non-main thread via m_PendingWindowTitle, flushed in
  OnUpdate (AppKit window operations are main-thread-only)

Compiler fixes (clang):
- EditorOperation.h: template keyword for dependent member templates
- TimeManager.cpp: std::chrono::zoned_time fallback for Apple Clang

Caveats / verify:
- imgui submodule moved from StudioCherno hazel-simpleux to luckyrobots/imgui
  dev. Confirm SimpleUX features noah/UI relied on are present in dev branch
  (or merge them into luckyrobots/imgui dev).
- 4 of the 24 source commits were "revert" commits that undid dev work
  inherited via PR #559; they're no-ops on noah/UI and were dropped.

commits.message:
Linux-Build.sh: drop dead lspgen step

The Ned editor was removed but the Linux build script still tried to
'make lspgen' and run the resulting binary against a metaModel.json under
Hazel/vendor/Ned (a submodule that no longer exists). With no premake
project defining the lspgen target, every Linux CI job has been failing
with "No rule to make target 'lspgen'" since the Ned removal.

Nothing in tree still consumes the lspgen output, so the build step is
just deleted.

fix: guard glb importer against invalid textures

Two crash sites in AssimpMeshImporter:
  - Malformed embedded PNG/JPG left width/height/format zero after
    ToBufferFromMemory failure, then fed into Texture2D::Create.
  - Raw embedded path passed Buffer(pcData, 1) while spec declared
    full mWidth*mHeight, causing a buffer overread in Texture2D.

  error-texture handle instead of constructing a new error texture
  per failure. Raw branch also sized correctly (W*H*4) and tagged
  RGBA

commits.subject: fix(AgentMessagesView): invalidate cached message height on tool-collapse toggle
commits.message:
fix(AgentMessagesView): invalidate cached message height on tool-collapse toggle

The per-message MessageCache fingerprint hashes (text_ptr, text_len,
content_width, !streaming) — it does NOT include tool-collapse state.
Toggling a tool call open/closed mutates the rendered height but left
the cached height intact, so:

- Messages that subsequently went offscreen advanced layout by the stale
  height, shifting all messages below them.
- Total height tracked for the autoscroll content_grew detection drifted
  from reality.

Fix: when the user clicks a tool-call header to toggle, mark the owning
message's cache entry invalid so the next frame re-measures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(AgentMessagesView): restore markdown for tool results + spinner streaming indicator
commits.message:
fix(AgentMessagesView): restore markdown for tool results + spinner streaming indicator

Two regressions exposed by the chat-consumer merge that didn't carry
over from mid::chat::ChatView:

- Tool results fell back to plain line-by-line AddText; mid called
  render_markdown_text. Restored by parsing tc.result into
  Markdown::Blocks and dispatching to RenderMarkdownBody, so headings,
  bold/italic, lists, and embedded code fences render correctly.
- Streaming indicator drew literal "..." text; mid had a hook the
  panel installed to draw an animated spinner. Restored by calling
  ImGuiEx::DrawSpinner inline (one consumer, no need for the hook
  indirection on the new Hazel-owned view).

To make tool-result text participate in selection cleanly,
RenderMarkdownBody and RenderCodeBlock now take (src_text, src_text_len,
identity_hash) explicitly instead of pulling them off a Message. This
fixes a latent bug in the existing tool-call code path where
RenderCodeBlock was passed tc.input/tc.result data but used msg.text
for selection offsets — selection ranges inside JSON tool input/result
were being computed against the parent message's text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(AgentMessagesView): port post-merge UX polish from mid::chat::ChatView
commits.message:
feat(AgentMessagesView): port post-merge UX polish from mid::chat::ChatView

mid::chat::ChatView was deleted on mick/chat-consumer; the same UX work
we'd landed in mid needs to live on AgentMessagesView. Ports:

- Theme::top_inset (<0 = auto 0.25*font_size; >=0 = exact pixels). Lets
  the agent panel reserve a top strip for its overlay buttons without
  the first conversation bubble bleeding under them.
- Tool calls default-collapsed; m_tool_collapsed lookup-absence now
  means "collapsed", not "expanded".
- Tool-call arrow: emoji triangle (U+25B6/U+25BC) replaced with
  geometric ImDrawList::AddTriangleFilled matching ImGui::RenderArrow
  so it renders identically to tree-node arrows and never falls back
  to a coloured emoji.
- Autoscroll: detect content_grew (height changes between frames, e.g.
  user expands a tool call) and window_shrunk (viewport reduces, e.g.
  a tool approval widget appears) on top of the existing
  at_bottom_now + new_message + streaming checks. Three new tracking
  members: m_last_total_height, m_last_render_size_y,
  m_was_at_bottom_last.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: more stable serialized transforms for MuJoCo entities
commits.message:
more stable serialized transforms for MuJoCo entities

Occassionaly the transforms of MuJoCo entities can drift slightly when serializing the scene
(even with the Init + Step(0) that we do for Motion and Animation graphs).
This drift causes a false positive in the scene dirty hash, with the result that the user sees spurious "this scene has unsaved changes" messages.
This commit makes Motion graph init + step(0) more deterministic (and hence less likely transforms of MuJoCo entities will drift).
Note: its possible similar fix needs to be applied to init + step(0) for Animation graphs - will deal with that when (or if) it occurs.

commits.subject: fix: mid pointer corruption in Agent panel
commits.message:
fix: mid pointer corruption in Agent panel

- Add monotonic AgentClient::Generation() counter (bumped at every
  m_Messages mutation) and replace the panel's SyncSignature
  dirty-check, which could collide between default-constructed sig and
  an empty conversation and silently render stale dangling pointers
  after Clear / LoadConversation / New.
- Exact simdjson ForEach count in CollectToolResults replaces the
  substring "id" heuristic. Reserves on m_ToolCallNames / Inputs /
  Results are now tight upper bounds — vectors never reallocate
  mid-build, so captured back().c_str() pointers (incl. SSO inline
  buffers for short tool names: Bash / Read / Edit) stay valid for
  the frame mid renders them in.
- Tighten m_RenderMessages + m_ToolResultStrings reserves by walking
  the build loop's skip predicates in pass 1 - exact, not upper-bound.
- Clear m_ImageThumbnails on LoadConversation (previously only Clear /
  New cleared it, so loaded conversations could flash stale images at
  matching message indices).
- Delete unreachable RenderImageThumbnails; latent in-frame
  dangling-pointer hazard if wired before m_View.render.

commits.subject: LocalClaude: always-on MCP, lock claude to mcp__editor__*, panel autosize
commits.message:
LocalClaude: always-on MCP, lock claude to mcp__editor__*, panel autosize

Ran into three issues during in-editor testing:

1. Auto-start was gated on `Backend == LocalClaude`, which only fires at
   boot. Toggling the radio after boot left the user with no MCP server
   and a confusing error. MCP now starts unconditionally on the loopback
   default ports — every backend benefits and external claude-code from
   a terminal also has somewhere to point.
2. The default 8765/8766 collided with a docker-proxy listener observed
   in the wild. Bumped to 19330/19331 (high, unusual range).

commits.subject: AgentClient: cancel curl before joining worker on shutdown
commits.message:
AgentClient: cancel curl before joining worker on shutdown

Follow-up to e2387daa3. The deferred-join via ReapWorkerAsync() is fine
when StreamThread has finished naturally — it's the cancel/destructor
paths (JoinWorker on Cancel(), SetMessages(), ~AgentClient(), and the
back-pressure case in ReapWorkerAsync where the previous slot still has
a live worker) that need a kick to libcurl, not just a join.

Without it, a worker sitting in curl_easy_perform on a stalled SSE
stream pins the UI thread for the full k_StreamTimeoutSeconds (300 s)
when SendMessage tries to start a new request — captured live via gdb,
stack:

  SendMessage:277 -> JoinWorker:158 -> m_PreviousWorkerThread.join()
                                       -> __pthread_clockjoin_ex
                                       -> ... worker still in curl_perform

Reproduced with claude-http-shim where the shim's stream-json output
sometimes doesn't close the SSE cleanly after the final assistant
message — curl keeps reading until k_StreamTimeoutSeconds.

Fix: in JoinWorker and the back-pressure branch of ReapWorkerAsync, set
m_CancelFlag.store(true) before .join(). StreamingHttpClient already
polls the flag from CURLOPT_XFERINFOFUNCTION and returns
CURLE_ABORTED_BY_CALLBACK, so curl unwinds within one progress tick
(milliseconds, not minutes).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: AgentClient: defer worker-thread join off the UI thread
commits.message:
AgentClient: defer worker-thread join off the UI thread

ProcessEvents() runs every frame on the editor's UI thread. The previous
StreamDone / Error branches called m_WorkerThread.join() inline — but
the worker is still inside curl_easy_perform() at that moment, possibly
for the remainder of k_StreamTimeoutSeconds (300 s). The OS shows
'Lucky Engine is not responding' within seconds.

Repro: configure any HTTP backend (Claude (Local) shim, OpenRouter,
etc.), send a message that ends in error or whose SSE stream stalls.
First seen with the claude-http-shim where claude -p's stream-json
sometimes doesn't close the SSE cleanly after the final assistant
message.

Fix: rotate the dying worker into a new m_PreviousWorkerThread slot
via ReapWorkerAsync() instead of joining inline. By the time the
*next* UI-side event triggers a reap, the previous worker has long
since returned from curl, so the deferred join() is instantaneous.
JoinWorker() (the synchronous shutdown path) reaps both slots so
nothing leaks at destructor time.

Closes #705

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Linux: $ORIGIN-relative rpath via Premake runpathdirs
commits.message:
Linux: $ORIGIN-relative rpath via Premake runpathdirs

Replace the cwd-relative -Wl,-rpath flags injected from
scripts/Linux-Build.sh with Premake's native `runpathdirs` API.
Premake's GCC toolset emits the absolute path as a $ORIGIN-relative
RUNPATH entry, so the editor binary now finds its Conan-shipped .so
files regardless of the launch cwd.

Before:
  LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold -Wl,-rpath=.,-rpath=bin,-rpath=.conan-Release/bin"
  $ readelf -d LuckyEditor | grep RUNPATH
  RUNPATH  Library runpath: [.:bin:.conan-Release/bin]

After:
  LDFLAGS="-fuse-ld=mold"
  $ readelf -d LuckyEditor | grep RUNPATH
  RUNPATH  Library runpath: [$ORIGIN/../../../.conan-Release/bin]

Verified ldd from /tmp resolves libparquet, libarrow, libdxcompiler,
libGFSDK_Aftermath, libvulkan, etc., all via $ORIGIN-relative path.

This drops Emily's "temporary fix" workaround (#674 comment) now that
runpathdirs is functional in the bundled premake5-beta7 for relative
paths. The upstream issue (premake/premake-core#2578) only blocks
absolute-path support, which we don't need here.

Closes #674

commits.subject: McpServer: add streamable-HTTP transport, drop Python stdio bridge (#681)
commits.message:
McpServer: add streamable-HTTP transport, drop Python stdio bridge (#681)

Adds HTTP MCP transport on `--mcp-http=PORT` (default --mcp+1) so claude-code
can talk MCP directly via streamable-HTTP per the 2025-03-26 spec — no broker
process between the LLM client and the editor. The existing TCP transport on
--mcp stays untouched; mcp_client.py still uses it for harness/* tools.

Engine
- Vendor cpp-httplib v0.18.5 (single-header, MIT) at Hazel/vendor/cpp-httplib/.
- New HttpTransport (PIMPL'd around httplib::Server) with POST /mcp,
  DELETE /mcp, GET /healthz, GET /version. Mcp-Session-Id header tracking
  with idle expiry. Bearer-token auth wired but unused (loopback unauthed
  default; AllInterfaces fail-closed without token at Start time).
- McpHttpConfig struct: bind scope, auth mode, idle timeout, worker cap.
- McpServer::Start now brings TCP and HTTP up together; either failing
  rolls back the whole server. McpServer::DispatchRpcLine factored out so
  both transports share the parse/dispatch/build path.
- Socket.cpp: extract ApplyReuseSockopts(int fd) so the HTTP listener
  picks up the same SO_REUSEADDR | SO_REUSEPORT setup TCP got in #682.
- LuckyEditor.cpp: parse --mcp-http=PORT (defaults to --mcp+1).

Harness
- claude_driver.py: emit {"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:PORT/mcp"}
  config; talk streamable-HTTP directly. Drop the stdio bridge subprocess.
- editor_lifecycle.py: pass --mcp-http=PORT, wait for both ports to bind.
- agent_loop.py: --http-port flag (defaults to --port+1).
- Delete tests/agent-eval/runner/mcp_stdio_bridge.py (~150 LOC).
- Update AGENT_LOOP.md and luckyengine-autotest SKILL.md.

Architecture doc
- New section 2.10.5 "MCP Harness Server" in LuckyEngine-Architecture.md
  covering both transports, threading model, extension points.

Validation: Release build clean. Live editor smoke test against
127.0.0.1:14838 — /healthz, /version, initialize (mints session id),
tools/list (49 tools), tools/call harness/get_agent_status (round-trips
through MainThreadDispatcher), ping, DELETE /mcp (204), notifications/*
(204). TCP regression check: 49 tools, tools/call works — unaffected.

commits.subject: llm_judge: capture and surface subprocess stderr on judge-error verdicts (#690)
commits.message:
llm_judge: capture and surface subprocess stderr on judge-error verdicts (#690)

When `claude -p` exits non-zero, the verdict reasoning was truncated to
300 chars without rstrip, and offered no fallback when stderr was empty
(some failure modes write only to stdout). Reviewers saw a literal
`stderr: ` with nothing after it and could not distinguish auth failure
from rate-limit from API hiccup.

Now we rstrip and cap stderr at 1000 chars, fall back to a stdout tail
when stderr is empty, and explicitly note when both streams are empty.

Closes #684

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: claude_driver: tolerate empty/truncated stream-json output (no more JSONDecodeError) (#691)
commits.message:
claude_driver: tolerate empty/truncated stream-json output (no more JSONDecodeError) (#691)

`claude -p` sometimes exits successfully but writes empty or truncated
stdout, causing the harness to crash with a JSONDecodeError that bubbles
out of the line-by-line parser and erases all signal from real agent
runs (some had 20+ tool calls in flight). This change wraps each
json.loads in try/except, logs malformed lines, and surfaces a
structured error on the transcript when 0 events parse — so the
validator gets a verdict and downstream steps (screenshots, scene state)
still run.

Closes #683.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: harness_create_project: substitute $SCRIPT_ASSEMBLY_NAME$ in scaffold templates (#694)
commits.message:
harness_create_project: substitute $SCRIPT_ASSEMBLY_NAME$ in scaffold templates (#694)

Walk the entire copied template tree after recursive copy and replace
placeholder tokens in BOTH file contents and filenames. Without this,
the per-file substitution missed any newly added template files and the
resulting projects shipped literal `$SCRIPT_ASSEMBLY_NAME$.sln`,
`$SCRIPT_ASSEMBLY_NAME$.csproj`, and a premake5.lua that still
referenced the placeholder — causing the scripting subsystem to fail
loading `Binaries/$SCRIPT_ASSEMBLY_NAME$.dll` and every script-based
agent scenario to hit BUILD_FAILED.

Substituted tokens: $PROJECT_NAME$, $DEFAULT_NAMESPACE$, $SCRIPT_ASSEMBLY_NAME$.
Substitution applied to file content + filenames for every file under the
copied template root.

Closes #670

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: McpServer: also set SO_REUSEPORT and log setsockopt failures (#682)
commits.message:
McpServer: also set SO_REUSEPORT and log setsockopt failures (#682)

SO_REUSEADDR alone covers TIME_WAIT but doesn't help when the kernel
hasn't fully reaped a prior process that crashed while holding the same
LISTEN socket. The autotest harness on Linux can crash the editor (see
#671) and immediately spawn a new one ~4s later — bind() then fails with
EADDRINUSE despite SO_REUSEADDR being set. Adding SO_REUSEPORT (Linux/
macOS only, guarded by #ifdef) bypasses the teardown window.

Also: previously the setsockopt return values were ignored. If either
call fails silently — say, the platform doesn't support the option for
this socket type — bind() would proceed without protection and we'd
have no visibility into why. Both calls now log a warning on failure.

Repro: https://ci.luckyrobots.com/jobs/201 (iter 319-78-gear-chain).
Fixes #680.

commits.subject: feat(data): Observer wires EpisodeReportStreamer; abort-poll between episodes
commits.message:
feat(data): Observer wires EpisodeReportStreamer; abort-poll between episodes

Per-episode HTTP no longer blocks the editor main thread.

- StartSession: after RecordingSession::Start succeeds, spawn the
  streaming worker with the new task's id + active-org snapshot.
- SubmitEpisodeToHub: pushes onto the streamer queue instead of calling
  RecordingSession::SubmitEpisode (which has been removed). Push() only
  blocks if the bounded queue is full (backpressure at the natural
  episode boundary, never drops).
- StartNextEpisode: polls m_Streamer.ShouldAbort() between episodes. A
  terminal Hub response on a previous submit (400 quota / 401 auth-expired
  / 402 payment / 403 permission) flips the streamer's atomic abort flag,
  the next poll triggers drain + StopTask + state=Idle, and the
  streamer's reason is logged for the user.
- StopSession + the TotalEpisodes-reached branch in StartNextEpisode:
  drain the streamer with a 5s timeout (drops pending past the deadline,
  in-flight HTTP still completes), then check the now-bool return of
  RecordingSession::Stop() so failed Hub stops surface a warn instead of
  dangling silently.

Bundled cleanup: removes the stale Tick() comment in CStartRecording
(Tick() was deleted in 4ea7540).

docs/recording-luckyhub-api-integration.md updated with the new state
machine, sequence diagram, class diagram, and 5 additional Key Design
Decisions (KDR 14-18) covering streamer ownership, backpressure-not-drop,
terminal vs transient classification, the 5s drain timeout, and the
single abort-poll site at the episode boundary.

Addresses the perf review on PR #603 (mickryley, 2026-04-27): per-episode
HTTP is off the recording hot path while Hub remains authoritative for
quota / auth / payment / permission via per-episode reporting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: refactor(data): RecordingSession drops SubmitEpisode; Stop returns bool
commits.message:
refactor(data): RecordingSession drops SubmitEpisode; Stop returns bool

Per-episode HTTP moves to EpisodeReportStreamer (wired in the next
commit). RecordingSession keeps only the synchronous Hub task bookends:
CreateLocalTask on Start, StopTask on Stop.

Stop() now returns bool — false on Hub stop failure with state restored
so the caller can retry. The previous void return was silently ignored
by Observer::StopSession, making the retry-restore branch in Stop() dead
code.

MapCreateError case 0 → case -1: HubHttpClient::Post returns -1 on
network failure, never 0, so the friendly "Could not reach LuckyHub"
branch was unreachable.

New GetTaskOrgId() accessor exposes the active-org snapshot Observer
needs to seed the streamer at session start.

Header doc updated to reflect the narrower responsibility.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(data): add EpisodeReportStreamer (jthread + bounded queue)
commits.message:
feat(data): add EpisodeReportStreamer (jthread + bounded queue)

Introduces the standalone streaming worker that will own per-episode
SubmitEpisode HTTP off the editor main thread. std::jthread +
bounded std::deque (cap=8) + 2 condition_variable_any: Push() blocks at
the episode boundary on full (backpressure, never drops); the worker
drains until queue empty + stop_token.

Response classification: 400/401/402/403 flag a terminal abort via
m_AbortRequested atomic + mutex-guarded reason string; 5xx and network
-1 log a warn and the worker keeps consuming. ShouldAbort() is a cheap
acquire-load for the producer to poll at episode boundaries.

StopAndDrain(timeout) signals stop, waits for the queue to drain, drops
pending submits past the deadline, and joins the worker. The in-flight
HTTP request still completes before the jthread joins.

Producer-side API (Start / Push / StopAndDrain / ShouldAbort /
GetAbortReason) is single-thread-only, contract documented in the
header. Not wired into Observer yet — done in a follow-up commit so this
one stays compile-only.

Design rationale captured in docs/recording-luckyhub-streaming-worker.md.

Addresses the perf feedback on PR #603 review (mickryley, 2026-04-27).

Replaces the per-frame Tick() polling + free-update registration in
Observer with a synchronous Start/Submit/Stop on the Scene-owned
RecordingSession. The new flow is:

  StartSession → session->Start (sync auth + CreateLocalTask) → on success
  immediately runs StartNextEpisode + DataRecorder/CameraRecorder
  StartSession + transitions to DataState::Recording. No deferred state.

Removed:
- Observer::Tick() and the TimeManager free-update registration that
  drove it. Free-updates aren't available in headless and are off by
  default for performance — this PR no longer forces them on.
- m_ApiGateway field + GetApiGateway() accessors.
- DataState::PendingApproval enum value (no transient state in the new
  flow). Verified no serialization callers exist.
- RecordingApiGateway.{h,cpp} entirely. Subsumed by RecordingSession,
  which is simpler (no thread, no queue, no atomics, no condvar).
- StopSession's PendingApproval cancel branch.

DataPanel migrated:
- "Waiting for LuckyHub approval..." spinner branch deleted (no waiting
  state in sync mode).
- "Waiting..." button branch deleted.
- canStop no longer checks PendingApproval.
- Status line collapses AwaitingAuth/AwaitingHub/Rejected into a single
  TaskFailed read from RecordingSession::GetLastError().

Refs PR #603 review:
- item 1: Hub plumbing lifted out of Observer.
- item 2: Tick / free-update polling removed.
- item 3: Worker thread / queue / cv removed by deletion (not modernised
  to jthread — sync model makes the whole apparatus unnecessary).
- item 4: SubmitEpisodeAsync → SubmitEpisode, StopTaskAsync → Stop.

commits.subject: feat(data): introduce RecordingSession subsystem (sync API)
commits.message:
feat(data): introduce RecordingSession subsystem (sync API)

Scene-owned subsystem that owns the LuckyHub task lifecycle for
recording. All HTTP calls (CreateLocalTask, SubmitEpisode, StopTask) are
synchronous on the caller's thread, matching the pattern already used by
HubUserClient and HubOrgClient. No worker thread, no queue, no atomics —
Start/Submit/Stop run at natural pause points (button clicks, episode
boundaries) where a brief block is acceptable.

Wired into Scene next to Observer/GrpcStepSystem with a Reset() on
OnRuntimeStop. Observer is not yet using it; that swap comes in a later
commit so this stays bisectable.

Design notes:
- Stop() failure restores taskId/state and surfaces TaskFailed so UI can
  offer a retry; previous behaviour silently dropped the taskId on any
  HTTP error.
- MapCreateError handles 5xx as a distinct branch (transient unavailable)
  rather than collapsing into the generic "rejected: HTTP 5xx" message.
- Header documents thread-safety contract: not thread-safe, main-thread
  only. C# script callers reach this via Observer's main-thread glue.
- Reset() vs Stop() distinction documented in header — Reset is local
  state clear (Scene tear-down), Stop talks to Hub.

Refs PR #603 review (item 1: lift Hub plumbing out of Observer; item 2:
direct sync call instead of Tick polling; item 3: drop manual threading;
item 4: rename Async; item 6: switch over status codes).

commits.subject: feat(hub): add HubJson header-only builder + migrate HubRecordingClient
commits.message:
feat(hub): add HubJson header-only builder + migrate HubRecordingClient

Replaces ostringstream + manual JsonEscape + manual brace bookkeeping in
HubRecordingClient with a fluent Object/Array builder. Centralises
brace/comma bookkeeping, escaping, and numeric precision so individual
call sites stop hand-rolling JSON.

Builder protections:
- Done() is single-shot — second call asserts in debug, no-op in release.
- Append-after-Done asserts.
- Double() uses round-trip precision (max_digits10) instead of the
  default 6-digit operator<<.

HubUtils::JsonEscape now takes string_view to avoid the std::string copy
when callers pass non-owning views.

Addresses PR #603 review item 5 (hand-rolled JSON is fragile).

Note: no unit-test harness exists for Hazel core yet, so misuse
prevention is enforced at runtime via HZ_CORE_ASSERT instead of via
tests. Standing up a test framework is out of scope for this PR.

commits.subject: fix(policy): skip pre-step qpos freeze when motion graph drives the joint
commits.message:
fix(policy): skip pre-step qpos freeze when motion graph drives the joint

SanitizeJointStateBeforeControl hard-freezes non-policy actuated joints to
qpos0 every substep when any policy slot is active, to stop unclaimed DOFs
drifting under external forces. With a motion graph feeding ctrl[] for
those same joints via RecalculateControls (Track B, commit 68a46f87c),
the freeze-to-qpos0 and the graph's IK-target ctrl fought each other and
produced large, constant reaction forces through the constraints — enough
to destabilize an adjacent policy (walker torso yanked backward, eventual
NaN). Clamp Obs For Unclaimed Joints did not help because the disturbance
was physical, not observational.

Gate the freeze on graphDrivesThisJoint = (qposAdr < pendingNq). When the
graph has produced a pending JointStates for a joint this tick, the ctrl[]
path owns it and the freeze skips. When it hasn't, the freeze still runs
and holds truly unclaimed DOFs steady.

Verified on G1 walker (legs + waist) + LimbIK motion graph (arms) — robot
holds pose, walks forward, arms track external IK target entities.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: feat(policy/editor): None preset and Ctrl+click subtract on Driven Joints
commits.message:
feat(policy/editor): None preset and Ctrl+click subtract on Driven Joints

Adds a None button and turns every preset button into an additive/
subtractive pair. Plain click replaces the current selection with the
preset's joints. Ctrl+click removes the preset's joints from the
current selection — when the current set is the empty-equals-all
sentinel we materialise to the full list first so subtraction is
well-defined. A hint line documents the Ctrl modifier.

commits.subject: feat(policy): let motion graph drive non-policy actuators
commits.message:
feat(policy): let motion graph drive non-policy actuators

Previously RecalculateControls bailed out entirely when any PolicySlot
was active, so the motion graph couldn't drive any joints on an entity
that had a policy running — legs-by-policy + arms-by-graph scenes
couldn't work even with disjoint DrivenJoints.

Replace the full bail with per-actuator gating. For joint actuators
whose target joint is claimed by an active policy, skip control
synthesis (PolicyApplier writes qfrc_applied there and the actuator
gains are already zeroed by NeutralizeActuatorsForTorquePolicy). All
other actuators — tendon-driven ones, joint actuators on unclaimed
joints — continue to receive graph-synthesized ctrl values. Applies
to both the jointStates-present and null-jointStates (hold) paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(policy/codegen): emit per-scene <Scene>PolicyIds.cs on save

On manual scene save, SceneSerializer now walks every
RobotControllerComponent, collects (slot.Name, slot.Id) pairs, and
emits <PascalScene>PolicyIds.cs into the active project's

commits.subject: fix(policy): wire ClampObservationForUnclaimedJoints through to inference
commits.message:
fix(policy): wire ClampObservationForUnclaimedJoints through to inference

The inspector toggle existed and was forwarded into the applier's
SlotRuntime, but no code actually consumed it — policies always saw the
raw physics state regardless of the flag. This defeated the plan's
coexistence story: a walker co-running with a croucher would observe
the croucher-driven waist/arm poses as 'its own last action', drift out
of distribution, and destabilise the gait.

BuildObservation now accepts a JointDrivenMask and a clamp flag. When
the flag is set and a mask entry is false, JointPosRel, JointVel, and
LastAction are zeroed at that joint index — the policy sees what it
would have seen during training when only it was driving the robot.

PolicyRuntime stores the flag (set per-sync by the applier) and forwards
it along with m_JointDriven. Default remains false so single-slot
robots are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(policy): PolicyApplier now honours PolicySlot.DrivenJoints
commits.message:
fix(policy): PolicyApplier now honours PolicySlot.DrivenJoints

The DrivenJoints whitelist was read from the scene, stored on the
applier, and never consulted by anyone. PolicyRuntime::ApplyControl
unconditionally wrote PD torque for every descriptor joint, so two
active slots with disjoint DrivenJoints still stomped each other on
every joint and Priority alone decided the winner.

Thread the mask into the runtime:

- PolicyRuntime::SetDrivenJointMask(names) builds a per-joint bool
  vector and rebuilds m_PolicyControlledJointIds so ControlsJointId()
  reflects only joints this slot actually writes.
- ApplyControl's PD loop skips joints where the mask is false —
  qfrc_applied for those DoFs is left for a sibling runtime or
  gravity-comp.
- PolicyApplier calls SetDrivenJointMask every sync, so inspector
  edits take effect without a descriptor reload.
- ApplyControl's gravity-comp pass now accepts a vector of other
  active runtimes (not just one overlay) and skips any DoF any of
  them claims. Supports >2 slots.

Observation-side masking (zero obs values for joints the slot doesn't
drive) is still a TODO — with this commit, outputs are masked but each
policy still sees the real state of joints the other slot is driving.
Policies trained in isolation may go out-of-distribution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
refactor(policy): flip PolicyApplier authoritative + delete IK-overlay (#587 commit 3/6)

PolicyApplier is now the sole writer to sim state for active policy slots.
PolicyInferenceNode::ControlCallback is a no-op stub (kept until Commit 5
deletes the node type). ShouldBypassMotionGraphForPolicy is gone; the
motion graph always runs.

Deletes the IK-overlay surface in one sweep:
- MujocoSceneInstance: Set/Add/RemoveGlobalIKActuator, IsIKOverlayEnabled*,
  IsJointIKOwned, IsPolicyControlledJoint, IsTorquePolicyAuthoritative,
  ApplyIKOverlayIfActive, ApplyPolicyControlIfActive, SetIKOwnership*,
  RebuildIKOwnershipCache, OnActuatorIKToggled, and backing storage
  (m_ActuatorUsesIK, m_ScriptOwnedActuators, m_IK*Cache, s_GlobalIK*).
- Physics/Mujoco/Policy.{h,cpp}: header stubbed; cpp reduced to
  HasActivePolicySlot, AnyActivePolicyControlsJointId, and the
  NeutralizeActuatorsForTorquePolicy / StabilizeFingerJointsForTorquePolicy
  pair (now queried against PolicyApplier instead of node statics).
- PolicyRuntime::ApplyControl: IsJointIKOwned skip removed.
- Command script glue: Set/Add/Remove IK methods kept as deprecated
  no-ops with a warning log until Commit 4 migrates the script API.
- MujocoActuator::UsesIK/SetIK stubbed (storage is gone; editor checkbox
  will be cleaned up when the UI moves to the new policy surface).

PolicyApplier.Apply now runs active slots priority-ascending: lowest
priority acts as primary (zeros qfrc_applied, grav-comps non-policy
DoFs); higher priorities run as overlays that overwrite only their
claimed joints. Single-slot robots hit the primary path.

commits.subject: feat(policy): add PolicyApplier + RobotControllerComponent.Policies (shadow mode)
commits.message:
feat(policy): add PolicyApplier + RobotControllerComponent.Policies (shadow mode)

Commit 2 of the Issue #587 refactor. Introduces the per-MujocoSceneInstance
PolicyApplier dispatcher, the PolicySlot data on RobotControllerComponent, and
the script glue scaffolding — all wired in alongside the legacy path so it can
be validated in shadow mode before becoming authoritative in Commit 3.

- PolicyApplier: non-singleton, keyed by (entity UUID, slot id). Owns a
  PolicyRuntime per active slot; syncs lifecycle, bridges commands from the
  legacy PolicyInferenceNode instance, and no-ops its writer path until the
  flip in Commit 3. Behind HZ_POLICY_APPLIER_SHADOW=1 it logs one-shot that
  shadow mode is live (full numeric parity wired in a follow-up).
- RobotControllerComponent gains Policies: vector<PolicySlot>. PolicySlot
  carries Id, Name, DescriptorPath, Active, Priority, DrivenJoints whitelist,
  and ClampObservationForUnclaimedJoints flag.
- SceneSerializer: round-trips Policies under the RobotControllerComponent
  block; forward-compat only in this commit (legacy scenes still work).
- SceneHierarchyPanel: adds a Policy Slots section with add/remove, all UI
  routed through ImGuiEx.
- MujocoSceneInstance: constructs one PolicyApplier per instance; calls
  Apply() after the legacy ApplyPolicyControlIfActive() in all three substep
  sites (SimulateControl, SimulateWithSubsteps, single-step Simulate).
  Caches owning Scene* from Rebuild so Apply can enumerate entities.
- Script glue: new RobotControllerComponent_{Set,Is}PolicyActive and the
  Set/Get Float/Bool stubs, all taking uint32_t ids. C# side gets methods on
  RobotControllerComponent plus a new Hazel.RobotController wrapper with
  enum overloads (Unsafe.As<TEnum, uint>, no boxing) so callers write
  robot.SetPolicyActive(PolicyIds.Walker, true) without manual (uint) casts.

The non-shadow write path is intentionally empty in this commit — the legacy
PolicyInferenceNode remains authoritative. Commit 3 flips the applier.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: refactor: extract PolicyRuntime from PolicyInferenceNode (#587 commit 1/6)
commits.message:
refactor: extract PolicyRuntime from PolicyInferenceNode (#587 commit 1/6)

Moves ONNX policy runtime state out of the motion-graph node statics into a
per-instance `Hazel::Policy::PolicyRuntime`. Supporting types split into
PolicyDescriptor (descriptor JSON loader), PolicyCommandStore (typed
alias-resolving command maps with overlay fallback), and
PolicyObservationBuilder (obs vector assembly).

PolicyInferenceNode becomes a thin wrapper that owns a PolicyRuntime and
forwards lifecycle + per-substep calls. All static Command.* surface
(Send/Get/RequestPolicy/RequestOverlayPolicy) is preserved and delegates
to the runtime through ResolveCommandTarget. Overlay fallback is wired
via CommandStore::SetFallback so overlay lookups still cascade to primary.

No behavior change — code moved verbatim with only mechanical accessor
substitutions. Builds clean in Debug x64.

Part of Issue #587 policy refactor (6-commit local series).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

2) MujocoSceneInstance::Instantiate() now uses Utils::ApplyWorldPoseToEntity instead of directly setting (world) transforms

Exclude editor camera pos when evaluating whether scene has changed

When evaluating whether or not the scene has changed for auto-save purposes, exclude the editor camera position.  Something as trivial as moving the editor camera should not trigger an auto-save (its debatable whether *editor* camera position even belongs in the scene)

commits.subject: More stable scene serialization
commits.message:
More stable scene serialization

- change MujocoSceneInstance::KinematicUpdate() to use mj_kinematics instead of mj_forward
- add new MujocoSceneInstance::ForwardUpdate() (calling mj_forward) for those features that need it

Result: scene serialization is no longer exhibits drift in mujoco body/geom positions because KinematicUpdate() is more deterministic.

commits.subject: Motion graph retargeting
commits.message:
Motion graph retargeting

MotionGraphs can now be instantiated on robots other than the one they were originally authored for.
In this case, any graph/node inputs that reference bodies or sites are remapped from the motion graph's original robot to the one that the graph is now being instantiated on.
Remapping is done by matching body/site names (there is no other way).
If a graph/node input cannot be remapped, then the graph cannot work on the new robot, and instantiation will gracefully fail.

commits.subject: Harden LuckyHub auth and HTTP stack against agreed security findings
commits.message:
Harden LuckyHub auth and HTTP stack against agreed security findings

SSL verification no longer disabled when CA bundle is missing, CSRF
state validation rejects empty pending state and clears after use,
shared mutable state protected with atomics/mutexes, detached threads
replaced with joinable members, HTTP headers sanitized against CRLF
injection, org IDs validated before URL construction, deep-link socket
uses XDG_RUNTIME_DIR with symlink check, token file created atomically
with 0600 permissions, and callback URL parameters are now URL-decoded.

commits.subject: Major refactor of IK solver to improve reliability (#462)
commits.message:
Major refactor of IK solver to improve reliability (#462)

- Add new joint limit avoidance logic (helps in two ways: 1) avoid moving to joint extremes in the first place, 2) can allow steps away from joint limits even if that moves away from IK target.
- Joint limit avoidance fades to nothing as target is approached (in case reaching the target really does require joints at limits).
- Unified objective function for convergence and result comparison (incl. joint limit penalties).
- Sort and prioritize restart seeds by initial error (aim is to investigate promising seeds first).
- Add post-restart single joint flips escape deep local minima.
- Use deterministic, low-discrepancy Halton sequences for restart seeds instead of random sampling.
  (note: this will make no difference with current low kMaxAttempts, but will be better in the event that kMaxAttempts ever needs increasing).
- Remove some obsolete code, and improve comments.

When a robot pack (e.g. Panda, Piper) is imported from the Content Vault,

stored Model handle doesn't match the actual MujocoScene, the handle is
updated, the graph is recompiled, and the asset is saved before creating
the instance.

Fix cross-pack asset registry path resolution

When loading .hzr registry files, paths were always treated as relative
to the registry file's directory. But ContentCreator generates paths
relative to the assets root (e.g. ContentVault/Environments/The Bungalow/...).
This caused cross-pack references to get a bogus prefix like
ContentVault/Examples/G1PickPlace/ContentVault/Environments/...

Fix: check if the path resolves directly under the assets root first
(cross-pack references). Only fall back to registry-relative resolution
for local pack assets (e.g. Meshes/foo.hsmesh).

commits.subject: Fix crash on heavy asset import (SM_Bungalow_Full.glb, 70+ textures)
commits.message:
Fix crash on heavy asset import (SM_Bungalow_Full.glb, 70+ textures)

Root cause: RenderCommandQueue::Allocate() was not thread-safe. The async
asset loading thread and main thread both called Renderer::Submit()
concurrently, racing on m_CommandBufferPtr and m_CommandCount. This
corrupted the command buffer, leading to garbage function pointers and
SIGTRAP/SIGABRT on Execute().

Fix: Add std::mutex to RenderCommandQueue::Allocate().

Additional defensive guards to prevent cascading crashes:
- Bounds checking in Allocate() with m_CommandBufferEnd pointer
- Null checks on Allocate() return in Submit() and SubmitResourceFree()
- Validate device->createTexture() return in Image2D::RT_Invalidate()
- Guard GenerateMips() against null image handles in Texture2D
- Guard CreateFromSRGB copy against null texture handles
- RT_CommitGraphicsState() returns false if pipeline is null
- Both RenderMesh overloads skip draw calls on pipeline commit failure

Texture size cap to reduce GPU memory pressure:
- Cap imported textures to 4096px max via stb_image_resize2
- Add stb_image_resize2.h vendor header (same family as stb_image)
- Downscale applied in both ToBufferFromFile and ToBufferFromMemory

commits.subject: Fix ContentVault zips baking absolute paths on Windows
commits.message:
Fix ContentVault zips baking absolute paths on Windows

Two fixes:

1. Windows CreateZip: use `cd /D parent && tar` instead of `tar -C parent`
   because Windows bsdtar silently ignores -C on long paths, causing full
   absolute paths (C:/Users/...) to be stored in the zip. Also use
   .ProviderPath instead of .Path in the PowerShell fallback to avoid
   potential PSPath provider prefix issues.

2. NormalizeExtractedRoot: walk down entire chain of single-child
   directories before flattening, not just one level. This handles zips
   that were already created with deeply nested absolute paths.

commits.subject: Replace ScaleAllSizes with _em literal for proper HiDPI scaling
commits.message:
Replace ScaleAllSizes with _em literal for proper HiDPI scaling

ScaleAllSizes() only covers ImGui's built-in style variables, leaving
hundreds of hardcoded pixel sizes in direct ImGui calls unscaled. This
caused visual mismatches between fonts and UI elements at non-1x scales.

Introduce a _em user-defined literal and emVec2() helper that multiply
by a global UI scale factor (contentScale/fbScale) at runtime. Convert
~233 callsites across 33 files to use _em/emVec2 so every pixel size
in the UI scales correctly with the display DPI.

commits.subject: fix: Moved ExternalActionGate -> SubSystem, added Scene Setting UI and Warning in gRPC Panel
commits.message:
fix: Moved ExternalActionGate -> SubSystem, added Scene Setting UI and Warning in gRPC Panel

To keep the TimeManager clean, and ensure we're not doing static calls when we don't need them, I moved the ExternalActionGate to a SubSystem. The only functional change is it will now block rather than escaping - so all gRPC calls will need to be off the main thread, and the C# calls no longer need to specify true/false on the action because it will strictly only permit 1 step at a time. If you open the gRPC Panel and the ExternalActionGate Subsystem hasn't been enabled there is a warning message with a quick-fix button. It's a subsystem controlled by a timerunner like any other - so it should always be on the same runner as the physics step, and running first (hence Acquisition -1000000 default) which you can confirm in the Scene Settings -> Execution Order panel

commits.subject: Add WASM port: MuJoCo physics + LeRobot v3 data recording in browser
commits.message:
Add WASM port: MuJoCo physics + LeRobot v3 data recording in browser

Complete implementation of Phases 0-2 and 4-5 of the WASM port:

- CMake build system compiling MuJoCo as static WASM library via Emscripten
- WasmMain.cpp: full simulation runtime with Panda robot loading, episode
  management, C API for JS interop, running statistics (Welford's algorithm),
  action/observation name generation from MuJoCo model
- JS data pipeline: data-export.js (LeRobot v3 format), storage.js (IndexedDB),
  episode-runner.js (session orchestrator), simulation-worker.js (Web Worker)
- 30 Playwright tests covering smoke, data recording, export, storage, E2E,
  and performance benchmarks — all passing
- Performance: ~12,000 physics steps/sec, ~97K episodes/hr, 27x real-time

Phase 3 (rendering) deferred: MuJoCo's mjr_* renderer uses OpenGL 1.5
fixed-function pipeline incompatible with WebGL2. Needs Three.js-based
renderer (documented in wasm-project.md).

commits.subject: Minor changes and cleanup to Mujoco Force Tool
commits.message:
Minor changes and cleanup to Mujoco Force Tool

- Mujoco Force Tool defaults to disabled.
- Enabled/disabled state persists across sessions (via app settings)
- MFT settings only appear in viewport settings menu in play mode
- MFT settings are disabled unless using editor camera (added a tool tip to tell you this)
- Apply torque is now SHIFT-left mouse drag (left mouse drag without shift is apply force)
- Removed unnessary code that switched which button did torque depending on which camera is active (MFT requires editor camera anyway)
- Replace EnsureExternalForceBuffer() with assertions (so we don't paper-over possible Mujoco model lifetime bugs)
- PendingBodyWrenchs now declared as float (double is unnecessarry, and its initialized from a glm::vec3  (which is float) anyway)
- Avoid leaking Mujoco.h header into rest of engine.
- Simplify application of forces in Simulate()
- Generalize and de-duplicate collider-to-body resolution for future maintainability (e.g. if new collider components added)
- Fix bad code indentation, and general format cleanups

Other:
- Fix ImGuiEx::IsItemHovered() not passing flags correctly

commits.subject: Mujoco Force Tool
commits.message:
Mujoco Force Tool

- Can be enabled or disabled in Viewport settings
- Works when using ejected editor camera in play/simulate
- Left click and drag on a mujoco object to apply force
- Middle click and drag on a mujoco object to apply torque
- Force values can be adjusted in Viewport settings

commits.subject: Fixes to the AO shaders. Improved the quality of the algorithm overall and unified it more with the standard xe-gtao.
commits.message:
Fixes to the AO shaders. Improved the quality of the algorithm overall and unified it more with the standard xe-gtao.

Fixed a Yflip on a view matrix, and fixed SSR shader to match that.

The GTAO shader now blurs more correctly, and when running at half res, it uses a better edge-detection algorithm to integrate better with the scene. Its still iffy, but its a clear graphical upgrade.

There is now a temporal noise property on the GTAO, this makes the
noise change, and can be used as a way to "preview" temporal noise before TAA is implemented.

There is also now a "Sample Count" property for the SSAO, this runs theinitial tracing N times. Its very expensive, but can be toggled on when making beauty screenshots.

The GTAO shader now creates its own depth mipmap, following the single-pass downsample the original XeGTAO did. This does increase memory, but it improves the quality from the AO as reusing the min/max HBZ from the other passes is the incorrect technique.

commits.subject: IK pole target + merge SegmentIK and LimbIK
commits.message:
IK pole target + merge SegmentIK and LimbIK

- merge the functionality of SegmentIK node into LimbIK node, and remove the SegmentIK node.
- add backwards compatibility code so that pre-exsting graphs using SegmentIK node are automatically mapped to LimbIK.
- add "Pole Target" input to LimbIK node.  This is a point in model-space that the IK seeks to align the bend plane of the chain with.
- "Pole Weight" input controls how strongly the IK tries to satisfy the pole target.  If zero, the pole target is ignored.

commits.subject: Fix MuJoCo dynamic objects slipping during simulation
commits.message:
Fix MuJoCo dynamic objects slipping during simulation

Skip syncing dynamic proxies from Hazel to MuJoCo during simulation.
MuJoCo should be the sole authority for dynamic object positions.

The TimeMaster changes introduced a round-trip sync (MuJoCo -> Hazel -> MuJoCo)
which interfered with contact force calculations, causing objects to slip
from the gripper. This restores the original one-way sync behavior where
MuJoCo drives dynamic object positions during simulation.

commits.subject: De-duplicate Mujoco mesh creation code
commits.message:
De-duplicate Mujoco mesh creation code

- Centralized MuJoCo mesh-to-StaticMesh logic in MeshFactory::CreateFromMujoco, replacing duplicated code in MujocoSceneInstance and Scene.
- Added MeshFactory::CreateWireframeBox for reusable wireframe box mesh creation, replacing manual edge mesh code.
- Meshsource for capsule collider debug meshes are now cleaned up on scene destruction.
- Removed some checking for IsAssetHandleValid(): GetAsset() with an invalid handle returns nullptr anyway, so checking IsAssetHandleValid() (which is not cheap) duplicates work.
- Minor white-space cleanup in SceneRenderer
