commits.subject: Mujoco Ned (#30)
commits.message:
Mujoco Ned (#30)

* Add Ned editor submodule and build system integration

- Add Ned as a git submodule in Hazel/vendor/Ned
- Update Dependencies.lua with libgit2 and curl paths for Ned
- Add libgit2 and libcurl to conanfile.txt
- Update premake5.lua files to include Ned in the build

* ScriptBuilder: Return build results with output capture

- Add ScriptBuildResult struct to capture success status and output
- Update Windows and Linux implementations to return build results
- Capture build output for error reporting

* VulkanImGuiLayer: Add ImGui font atlas hot-reload support

- Add HandleFontReload() to check for and process font changes from Ned
- Add RebuildFontAtlas() and UploadFontAtlasToGPU() for Vulkan font upload
- Update ImGuiFonts with GetFontConfig() and AddFontFromConfig() helpers

* Viewport: Add screenshot capture functionality

- Add CaptureScreenshot() method for PNG export
- Uses stb_image_write from GLFW deps for encoding

* Integrate Ned AI editor with LuckyEditor

- Add NedEditorLayer to manage Ned embed lifecycle
- Implement HazelAgentInterface with MCP tools for scene/entity manipulation
- Add AgentToolRegistry for tool registration and dispatch
- Integrate ContentBrowser with Ned for asset path operations
- Wire up EditorLayer to initialize Ned and sync active scene
- Update imgui.ini with Ned panel layout

* Update Ned submodule and rename Editor to Text Editor in content browser

* Update Ned submodule and imgui.ini

* Fix agent not having access to auto-loaded scene

* Add layout switcher with View menu and keybinds

* Add Ned text editor and agent visibility toggles to View menu

* Fix file sharing violation and update layouts

- Use FILE_SHARE_READ in TryOpenFile to prevent conflicts with OmniSharp LSP
- Update editor layout ini files

* Add prefab creation and scene management tools for AI agent

- Add PrefabCreationTools for creating prefabs from entities
- Add createScene callback for creating fresh scenes
- Add createPrefabFromEntity callback
- Fix OmniSharp scanning issue by pointing to Scripts folder instead of project root
- Update Ned submodule with new tools and bug fixes

* Update Ned submodule with syntax highlighting and agent UX fixes

* Add createMaterial tool and auto-delete prefab templates

- Add MaterialCreationTools for agent material creation
- Wire up createMaterial callback in HazelAgentInterface
- Auto-delete template entity after prefab creation
- Update Ned submodule (agent prompts, docs, hover fixes)

* Add MuJoCo collider support to agent tools

- Add MujocoBoxCollider, MujocoSphereCollider, MujocoCapsuleCollider to addComponent/removeComponent
- Create MujocoPropertySetter for setting Dynamic, Density, Friction, Contype, Conaffinity
- Add MuJoCo component serialization to getEntityProperties
- Add ParseInt helper to AgentHelpers
- Update Ned submodule with MuJoCo collider documentation

* Add entity hierarchy management tools for agent

- Implement ParentEntity, UnparentEntity, and ReorderChildEntity in EntityManipulationTools
- Wire up callbacks in HazelAgentInterface
- Update Ned submodule with MCP tool registrations

* Update Ned submodule - add close buttons to windows

* Add createGameObject tool and improve agent defaults

- Add GameObjectCreationTools for high-level game object creation
  (entity + mesh + material + collider + prefab in one call)
- Update Ned submodule with createGameObject MCP tool registration
- Increase default PointLight radius from 10 to 50 for better visibility
- Wire up createGameObject callback in HazelAgentInterface

* Update Ned submodule with agent-rules.txt support

* Add default Camera and Light to createScene

createScene now automatically creates Camera and Light entities with
TOP-DOWN game defaults. Also updates Ned submodule with docs update
and default model change to claude-sonnet-4.5.

* Update Ned submodule

* Update Ned submodule

* Update Ned submodule

- Fix BOM handling for cursor movement and selection rendering
- Add LSP diagnostics and hover toggle settings

* Update Ned submodule - fix hover symbol info triggering past end of line

* Update Ned submodule to vulkan-hazel branch

* Add HTTP GET/POST bindings for C# scripts

Adds Http static class with Get and Post methods for making HTTP requests
from C# scripts. Uses libcurl for the underlying implementation.

Example usage:
  string response = Http.Get("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1");
  string response = Http.Post("https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts",
                              "{\"title\": \"Test\", \"body\": \"Hello!\", \"userId\": 1}");

Both methods also support custom headers via an optional parameter.

* Update Ned submodule - disable conflicting keybinds and add reasoning tokens

* Update Ned submodule to latest

* Remove Dynamic property from Ned agent mujoco code

* Add MuJoCo component support and update prefab tools for new sync system

- Add support for MujocoCylinderCollider, MujocoMeshCollider, MujocoJoint components
- Update MujocoPropertySetter with properties for new components
- Fix GameObjectCreationTools and PrefabCreationTools to keep entities as linked
  prefab instances (don't delete after prefab creation)
- Update Ned submodule with Jenga/Domino doc fixes and preset prompt updates

* Remove layout switcher feature

- Remove Layouts/ folder and restore imgui.ini
- Remove layout switching code from EditorLayer (View menu, Ctrl+Shift+1-9 keybinds)
- Keep imgui.ini at root level as before

* Update Ned submodule with AI fixes, fix prefab creation crash

* Merge mujoco branch into mujoco-ned

Brings in nvrhi renderer backend, updated ImGui system, and various
engine improvements from the mujoco branch.

* Ned editor integration fixes for renderer 2025

ImGuiRenderer.cpp/h:
- Add global texture registry with per-renderer GPU texture copies
- New renderers sync existing textures via SyncGlobalTextures()
- Fixes NVIDIA crash when sharing textures across ImGui viewports
- Store owned texture handles to prevent premature destruction
- Convert asserts to graceful skips for missing/invalid textures
- Add error handling with try/catch around nvrhi texture operations

ImGuiLayer.cpp:
- Integrate Ned fonts via AddNedFontsToAtlas() before atlas build
- Add LoadHazelFonts() helper for font reload support
- Handle font atlas rebuild when Ned requests font reload

NedEditorLayer.cpp/h:
- Update editor layer for Ned embedded mode integration

Ned submodule:
- Updated to e0b775c3 with Hazel compatibility fixes

* Update imgui.ini layout

* Move agent tools to Ned submodule

Agent tools now live in Hazel/vendor/Ned/agent/ but are compiled by
LuckyEditor (which has access to Hazel dependencies).

This reduces the PR size by moving ~4600 lines to the Ned submodule.

* Make ImGuiRenderer persistent textures static for multi-viewport support

- Changed m_PersistentTextures to static s_PersistentTextures so textures
  are shared across all renderer instances (same pattern as s_FrameTextures)
- Made RegisterPersistentTexture a static method
- Increased PersistentHandleCount from 64 to 512 for Ned's icon textures
- Simplified HazelTextureManager to directly use static registration
- Updated Ned submodule with viewport lock removal for draggable windows

* Fix bad merge in SceneHierarchyPanel ScriptComponent handling

The previous merge incorrectly duplicated code inside the
PropertyScriptReference if-block, causing nested duplicate logic.
Restored the correct version from mujoco.

* Update Ned submodule to use public repo

commits.subject: Improve robustness of Motion Graph IK solver
commits.message:
Improve robustness of Motion Graph IK solver

- Refactor the Motion Graph IK restart logic to use a systematic sequence of start poses (current pose, mirrored, perturbed home, and finally wide perturbations) for up to 10 attempts.  This increases the chance of finding the globally optimal solution (e.g. if one or more of the start attempts gets stuck in local minima).
- Move solver hyperparameters (thresholds, iteration limits) to static constants in the Mujoco namespace and remove per-instance copies.
- Standardize threshold usage, clarify comments, and improve solution selection logic.

commits.subject: Refactor MujocoSceneAsset: asset/instance split, fixes race conditions
commits.message:
Refactor MujocoSceneAsset: asset/instance split, fixes race conditions

Major refactor of Mujoco scene management:
- Introduce MujocoSceneInstance to hold per-entity/scene simulation state, decoupling it from MujocoSceneAsset.
- MujocoSceneAsset now only manages immutable asset data (XML, actuators, etc.) and no longer owns simulation state or methods.
- All simulation logic (reset, simulate, actuator control, etc.) moved to MujocoSceneInstance.
- Whenever an entity with a MujocoSceneComponent is copied, then a new MucjocoSceneInstance is created,
  so multiple entities (potentially in different scenes) can all refer to the same MujocoSceneAsset without interference.

This fixes race condition (resulting in crash) when building asset pack.
Also means "editor" scene is more cleanly separated from "runtime" and "simulation" scenes
(e.g. nothing that happens in Mujoco for runtime scene can affect editor scene)

Other:
- Asset pack build cleaned up in general, in particular fix crashes if user tries to build asset pack again before previous build is complete.

commits.subject: New MotionGraph nodes
commits.message:
New MotionGraph nodes

- RestPose: outputs the rest pose ([0]th key frame, or qpos0) of a robot
- StoredPose: when triggered, stores current pose of the robot and then subequently outputs that stored pose every frame.  Outputs a given default pose if not triggered.
- MinJerkCurve: a maths node that when triggered outputs values from 0 to 1 over a given duration.  The values follow a minimum jerk quintic polynomial.

- Remove potential for SetJointStatesFromRest/Current/Pose to write to out-of-bounds memory
- data members for axis conversion quats since they are used in so many places - saves recreating them all the time, and reduces code duplication.

commits.subject: Split simulation step
commits.message:
Split simulation step

Split the mujoco simulation step into step1 and step2.
Allows to apply bias in between the steps so that control is compenstated for gravity (stops models from "drooping" during simulation)
The bias is applied only to joints that are actuated, so other joints (in particular free joints) will still be affected by gravity.

commits.subject: RobotControllerComponent + MotionGraph
commits.message:
RobotControllerComponent + MotionGraph

Basic framework for RobotControllerComponent and Motion graph is added in this commit.
RobotControllerComponent is intended to be added to added to an entity with a MujocoSceneComponent.
RobotControllerComponent references a MotionGraph.
MotionGraph is a node-graph that will be executed every frame to produce joint states for the mujoco model referenced by the graph.
Thus the mujoco model receives new joint states each frame, and is "animated".

Note: Later, the controller component will have additional (optional) functionality to convert the joint states produced by the graph into control values for the mujoco model's actuators.

commits.subject: "auto" animation state machine transitions
commits.message:
"auto" animation state machine transitions

Add option for animation state machine transitions to be "automatic".
This means that once the source state has played to completion, then the transition will automatically occur.
Example use case: Character is running then comes to a sudden stop. You want to play the "sudden stop" animation clip, and then when that's done, automatically resume the "locomotion" blend space.
While this was possible to do previously, it was extremely fiddly to set up.  With "auto" its as simple as ticking one box.

Change transition graphs "Transition" output from a boolean value to a "trigger", because:
- it makes a bit more sense. The transition is "triggered" (as opposed to it continually happens while the input is true)
- it better distinguishes the "Transition" pin from the new "Auto" pin.

commits.subject: GAME BREAKING CHANGE - uniform anim scale
commits.message:
GAME BREAKING CHANGE - uniform anim scale

Animation transform now has a single float for scale (instead of vec3).
This reduces the size of animation poses, and hence improves efficiency.  There is very little chance we ever need non-uniform scale in skeletal animation.

This change breaks previously baked games (if they have animation) (unavoidable, sorry) - please rebuild those games from the editor before trying to run them through the runtime.

Animations and AnimationGraphs are now linked to a Mesh instead of rig asset (and take the skeleton to animate from the mesh).

commits.subject: Poor mans animation retargeting (step 1)
commits.message:
Poor mans animation retargeting (step 1)

Animation graph nodes will now automatically retarget animations to their graph's skeleton.
The retargeting is based on a simple mapping of bones from source to target skeleton.
It will only work if:
- A mapping can be determined (currently it just maps on bone name, stripping any colon-delimited prefixes).
- The source and target have similar structure and similar proportions.
Root motion is not retargeted (source root motion is played as-is on target).

A nice side-effect of this is reduced size of compressed animation data, and slightly faster sampling of that data
(because non-animated tracks such as joint translations are no longer stored).

commits.subject: Angular velocity improvements and fixes
commits.message:
Angular velocity improvements and fixes

- Use a vec3 for angular velocity instead of a quaternion (as the latter does not allow for more than one revolution per second).
  The vector stores the axis of rotation, and the magnitude of the vector is the speed of rotation in radians per second.
- During scene update, do scripts first, then physics, then script late update.
  This means that if scripts move physics objects, then physics will "see" this in the same frame as the scripts (as opposed to the following frame)
  This in turn means phyics is using same delta time as the script update.
  (downside is that scripts will now not "see" physics collisions until the next frame)
- Fix incorrect Vector3.DirectionFromEuler() implementation.

commits.subject: improved root motion + bug fixes
commits.message:
improved root motion + bug fixes

- Improved handling of root motion when the user chooses _not_ to create a root bone on animation import.
  In other words, they want to use the animation asset's root bone as is.
  The animation asset root bone might not be at origin (notably mixamo has the "hips" as the root bone).
  The animation asset may have some rotation component applied to that root bone.
  This commit deals with these situations, allowing seamless use of these animations with ones that
  did have a new root bone created on import.
- Attempt to preserve speed when blending root motion between animations.
- Fix bug in blend space where incorrect animations were blended if all blend space vertices happen to be colinear

commits.subject: content browser bug fixes and performance boost
commits.message:
content browser bug fixes and performance boost

- implement a way for asset manager to determine asset dependencies _without_ having to load the entire asset
- including de-registering dependencies if/when they are no longer there (e.g. material ceasing to use a texture)
- use asset dependencies in ThumbnailCache so that it doesnt have to fully load all the assets to determine the asset time stamps
- use asset dependencies to ensure material thumbnails are regenerated if any texture that they depend on is changed
- use asset dependencies in meshsource thumbnail generation to avoid creating memory-only assets that duplicate already-existing assets
- make sure meshsource thumbnail generator will use an already loaded asset before trying to load (or create) a new one
- fix bug where meshsource thumbnail generator did not properly clean up the thumbnail scene afterwards

commits.message:
Remove 100 bone limit on animated entities

Size of bone transforms array for animated entities is now dynamically determined and can be different for each entity.
There can be as many bones as you like in the skeleton.
Only the bones that are used for skinning are actually uploaded to GPU.
There is still an overall limit of (1024 * 50) bone transforms (used for skinning) over all entities in total, and the GPU bone transform buffer is pre-allocated to this size.
(note: Previously it was 1024 * 100, so this is now half the size it was before)

commits.subject: Animated model loading improvements
commits.message:
Animated model loading improvements

- When loading a source asset with animation, create a "bone" for any animated node (even if that node is not used for skinning). See code comments for more details.
- If an asset has multiple root "bones", then step up the node hierarchy until we find a common ancestor, and make _that ancestor_ the root bone.  Thus skeletons in Hazel now always have exactly one root bone.  This is required for skeleton transform to work properly.
- Check on import that number of bones does not exceed the MAXBONES supported by Hazel.  Mark asset as invalid if so.
- When instantiating a mesh into the scene hierarchy, do not ignore root node if it also happens to be the root of the skeleton of a rigged mesh.
- Remove obsolete AssimpMeshImporter::ImportSkeleton()

commits.subject: Async asset system stability improvements
commits.message:
Async asset system stability improvements

This commit fixes several non-reproducible crashes that I strongly suspect were due to failure to synchronize data access between the main thread and asset thread.

- When loading an asset asynchronously, if that load in turn attempts to load an asset then that secondary asset will now be loaded into the asset thread's asset list so that correct sync back to main thread asset list occurs.
- If the asset thread queues events to be processed (on main thread) later, then processing of those events is now guaranteed to happen _after_ the asynchronously loaded assets have been sync'd to the main thread.
- Memory-only assets no longer have entries in the asset registry, and access to the memory only asset list is synchronized across threads.  This means that memory only assets can now safely be added at any time from any thread.
- Add AssetRegistry::SetMetadata() API to facilitate thread-safe modification of asset metadata.
- Remove non-thread safe GetMutableMetadata() and the (duplicated functionality) GetMetadataInternal()
- Many potential race conditions fixed - non-obvious code that is the way it is for thread-safety is commented.

Other:
 - Replaced IsMemoryAsset() with GetMemoryAsset().  This saves doing two lookups in situations where you want to get the asset immediately after determining that it is indeed a memory-only asset.
 - Now using asset dependency system to ensure Mesh/Staticmesh/Skeleton/Animation assets are reloaded if/when the underlying MeshSource is modified
 - Removed AssetRegistry::GetMetadata(Asset)  (use GetMetadata(asset->Handle) instead).  This simplifies the API and so reduces the potential to introduce errors later.
 - Remove "allowMemoryOnly" option from AssetSearchPopup as this is no longer possible now that memory assets are not in asset registry (this option was not used in any way that worked correctly anyway)
 - Remove variations on AssetSearchPopup(). Reduced API surface area and reduced code duplication = less potential for introducing errors.

commits.subject: Physics Improvements - GAME BREAKING CHANGES
commits.message:
Physics Improvements - GAME BREAKING CHANGES

Breaking changes:
- Teleport() method is removed from RigidBody component.
- To "teleport" an entity, you simply set its translation and or rotation.  This is the same irrespective of whether the entity has a rigidbody (of any type) or a character controller.
- To move an entity via physics (i.e. not teleporting), then use the appropriate method on the physics component (e.g. RigidBody.AddForce(), RigidBody.MoveKinematic(), CharacterController.Move() or whatever)

General improvements:
- Kinematic physics bodies now have their physics world positions synchronized with Hazel world position during the physics simulation.
- CharacterController component has new properties to control whether movement/rotation can be player controlled while the character is in air.
- CharacterController will automatically apply appropriate horizontal "momentum" when character is in air (assuming player control while in air is turned off)
- Added Rotate() method to CharacterController component (mirroing kinematic body Rotate()).
- SetRotation(quat) on TransformComponent is now much less likely to produce 180 degree flips in the Euler angle representation of the rotation.
- Add RotationQuat property to TransformComponent and a shortcut to it on Entity
- Add Conjugate property to C# Quaternion

Other
- Re-save Projectile.hprefab as it seems to have lost the reference to explosive particle

commits.subject: Improvements to JoltCharacterController
commits.message:
Improvements to JoltCharacterController

- refactored the update of character controller components to be more similar to the "CharacterVirtual" sample in Jolt physics repo.

- JoltContactListener and PhysicsContactCallback APIs now deal with entity ID's rather than Entity objects (this is more efficient, and removes duplication of scene->TryGetEntityWithID())

commits.subject: Improved animation synching + fix non-looping
commits.message:
Improved animation synching + fix non-looping

- Improvements to synching between RangedBlend or BlendSpace nodes and <other node>
  If a RangedBlend node is not synching between it's animations, then it will now sync the first animation with <other node> during transitions.
  Ditto BlendSpace nodes:  if one (or more) vertices aren't being synched, the remaining ones that are being synced will now be synched with <other node> during transitions.
  Synching is still done on a full animation duration basis, there are not yet time-ranges or sync markup within animations.
- Fix for non-looping animations. They now correctly don't loop, and emit the Finished event.
- RangedBlend node can now loop (or not) animations A and B independently.

commits.subject: tidy up checking for asset validity
commits.message:
tidy up checking for asset validity

AssetManager::GetAsset<>() now returns either a valid asset or nullptr
This means that if you get a non null pointer back, then the asset is good to be used.
This removes the need to check things like asset->IsValid(), or asset->IsFlagSet(AssetFlag::Missing()) etc. which in turn cleans up some inconsistency in the code (some people were checking those things, and some were not)

commits.subject: Reduce calls to AssetManager::GetAsset<>()
commits.message:
Reduce calls to AssetManager::GetAsset<>()

AssetManager::GetAsset<>() is:
a) expensive
b) not thread-safe
So this commit aims to remove as many calls to AssetManager::GetAsset<> as we can, and especially remove AssetManager access from things that potentially happen on the Render thread.
Do this by retrieving a Ref<MeshSource> as high up the call stack as we can, and then pass it down (rather than AssetManager::GetAsset<MeshSource>() deep in the call stack.

Other:
- Removed not-used Renderer2D::DrawAABB(Ref<Mesh>, ...).  This also de-couples Renderer2D from Mesh
- Added Entity::TryGetComponent<>() rather than doing extra work with HasComponent<>() followed by GetComponent<>()

commits.subject: replace Ref<Asset> data members with AssetHandle
commits.message:
replace Ref<Asset> data members with AssetHandle

So that:
- reloading an asset does not leave you with orphans (e.g. other classes holding onto Ref<Asset> mean that the old asset stays alive).
- reloading an asset means classes referring to that asset (via AssetHandle) immediately see the newly reloaded asset.

Other:
- remove unused GetMemoryOnlyAssets
- remove unused Mesh::Mesh(Ref<Mesh>) constructor.
- remove unused StaticMesh::StaticMesh(Ref<StaticMesh>) constructor.
- note: the two constructors removed did not treat material table correctly either.
- refactor duplicated code in SceneHierarchyPanel::DrawEntityCreateMenu() into a lambda

commits.subject: PBR material import fixes
commits.message:
PBR material import fixes

- When importing materials via assimp:
  - look for albedo in AI_MATKEY_BASE_COLOR property first.
    only use aiTextureType_DIFFUSE if BASE_COLOR is not found.

  - look for roughness in AI_MATKEY_ROUGHNESS_TEXTURE first.
    Only use aiTextureTYPE_SHININESS if ROUGHNESS is not found
    If using shininess texture, then set roughness 1 - shininess

  - (currently disabled) If explicit metalness texture is not found, then use roughness texture.

  - metalness value clamped to either 1.0 or 0.0 as physically correct materials
    are either metal or they are not.

  - look for metalness texture in AI_MATKEY_METALLIC_TEXTURE

    Per GLTF spec. metalness is in B channel and roughness in G channel.

  - fix compilation errors if MESH_DEBUG_LOG is defined to 1

commits.subject: Animation graph events raised to game scripts
commits.message:
Animation graph events raised to game scripts

- Added new "Event" output node.  When triggered, these nodes will place an event in the animation graphs "OutgoingEvents" queue.
- Scene "UpdateAnimation" function dequeues items from the OutgoingEvents queue and raises them as events in any script component attached to the same entity.
- Added new "Bool Trigger" nodes.  These nodes evaluate a boolean input and raise an OnTrue event or an OnFalse event as appropriate.
- Animation graph events are raised in script component attached to same entity as the animation component.  This means that in a scene, the animation component can no longer be on a child of the entity that has the script component.
  Reworked "AnimationTest" and "AnimationStressTest" scenes so that the animation component is no longed on a child of the "Player" entity.
- Added example animation events to the "Player" animation graph, and an example handler to the ThirdPersonAnimated C# script.

Other
- Fix bug with wrong IDs calculated for graph input variable names consisting of multiple words delineated by captial letter (e.g. "ForwardsState" now works correctly as an input name).
- Added SetRotation() API to physics character controller.
- Replaced GetSpeedDown() on physics character controller with GetLinearVelocity() (and added a SetLinearVelocity() also).
- Expose IsGravityEnabled property of physics character controller to C# game scripts.
- Improved stability (in some cases) when setting an entity's Rotation (euler angles).
- Removed "Root Motion Target" from Animation Component.  The target for root motion is now always assumed to be the entity that has the animation component.
- GraphSerializer will now attempt to read input data where the topology does not match factory nodes.
  This allows for changes to be made to nodes, but still be able to read pre-existing graphs.
  It is not perfect.  Matching is done based on pin names.  If pin types change, it likely will not work.
- removed GetRandom<> nodes for animation graph.
- Fix copy-paste mistake in ScriptGlue.cpp ErrorWithTrace().

commits.subject: Revert "WIP:  Variable setter + trigger nodes"
commits.message:
Revert "WIP:  Variable setter + trigger nodes"

This reverts commit 798e34bc9a4ddc1d9fe8b4bc7c7eb6c49029121b.
While the code from that commit did work, it blurs lines of responsibility between systems.
The job of an animation graph is to generate a pose and that's it.  Nothing else.
The variable setter + trigger nodes made it possible to make the animation graph do things that should be really be "game logic".
So, in the interests of keeping clear separation of concerns (animation graph does poses, game logic is done by scripting) I am removing the variable setter and trigger nodes from the animation graph.
We don't want that.

commits.subject: WIP:  Variable setter + trigger nodes
commits.message:
WIP:  Variable setter + trigger nodes

Local variables are now local to animation graph instance (used to be local to each sub-graph within the instance)
Setting a local variable is now a node in the runtime graph (used to be a short-circuit)
These two changes allow some interesting use cases, such as setting a local variable value in one sub-graph, and reading that value in another sub-graph.

Added trigger nodes back.

Still todo:
- put back "input action" for anim graphs so that trigger nodes can be triggered when a graph is instantiated.
- output events (at least for sub-graphs). e.g. so that starting a transition could trigger, say, a counter.
- local variables of type trigger  (so that one subgraph can trigger a node in another subgraph)

commits.subject: Fix problems with red error outlines in animation graph
commits.message:
Fix problems with red error outlines in animation graph

Comment nodes in animation graph would be outlined in red (i.e. error) if the comment happened to be "State Machine".
Ditto local variable nodes in animation graph would be outlined in red (error) if the variable name happened to be "State Machine".
The fix is to move the comment to be stored in the node Description field instead of node Name (likewise local variable node now stores the variable name in node->Description)

I have not changed sound graph local variable nodes.  They still use node.Name to store the name of the local variable.
I have changed sound graph comment nodes to store comment in node.Description (because the editor-side code that renders these nodes is shared with anim graph)

commits.subject: Copy and Paste for animation graph nodes
commits.message:
Copy and Paste for animation graph nodes

Select one or more nodes in animation graph (or subgraphs) right click and you can now "Copy" from the context menu.
Right click somewhere else (or in a different subgraph) and you can now "Paste" the copied nodes.
Useful for quickly setting up state machine graphs where transition sub-graphs are all very similar (so just Copy/Paste them)

Other:
- When a new transition is created, automatically add an output node
- Fix bug that allowed creation of a transtion between a node and itself
- Right clicking a node now selects the node (if it is not selected already)
- You can now have multiple "setter" nodes for the same local variable - so long as they are in different sub-graphs (each subgraph has its own copy of the local variables)
- Tweaks to definition of "IsWellDefined" for a node:
  - Asset handle input pins must not be null
  - Pose input pins must be connected
- rename GetSelectedNodes() -> GetSelectedNodeIDs() since it is returning a vector of IDs
- remove ASSERT from NodeEditorModel. This was firing for conditions that can happen normally during deletion of nodes from a graph

commits.subject: Animation Graph working mvp - Feature parity with Animation branch!
commits.message:
Animation Graph working mvp - Feature parity with Animation branch!

GAME BREAKING COMMIT
If your game project contains animation, this commit will break it.
After updating to this commit you need to:
* Delete all Hazel Animation and AnimationController assets, and then re-create them by dragging the raw DCC files into your scene.  Be sure to tick the "Create Animation Controller" box, and pay attention to the new Root Motion Mask settings in the import UI.

* Re-assign the newly generated AnimationController(s) to your animated characters as appropriate.

* Re-compile game C# scripts, fixing any compile errors that will now happen:
   * Setting AnimationTime via script is no longer supported
   * Setting RootMotion enable/disable flag via script is no longer supported
   * Setting "State" via script is no longer supported (replace this with the SetInputInt() API, passing in an identifier for the "State" graph input).  Refer example ThirdPerson.cs script in Sandbox.

Changes:
- Complete re-write of AnimationController to now be based off node-graphs.  Code (sort-of) shared with SoundGraphs (still lots of tidy up to do to better share this code))

- Re-write animation asset import.
   - An AnimationAsset now refers to one animation clip only. (Raw DCC can still contain multiple animations, these will just be split into several independent AnimationAssets)
   - Root motion masking (if any) is now done during import, rather than at runtime.

- Allow node graphs with no setter node for local variables (in this case, the variable value is taken from the default value)

- The (float) value sent into a node graph via SendInputEvent() now propagates through the graph.
   This is used to send in timedelta for animation graph update.

- Add support for node graphs to generate any type of output (not just floats), so long as that output can be stored in a choc::value::Value

- Implement the SampleAnimation node:  Upon receipt of Update event, steps time forwards and output root motion and pose sampled from a given AnimationAsset

- Move Utils out of Hazel/Audio/SoundGraph/GraphGeneration.cpp so that can be used also by animation graph

- Many other changes to support use of node graphs for animation…

Nothing in SoundGraphs should be broken by this commit

Temporary fix to prevent crash with dynamic mesh

Manually assigning a mesh to an entity's Mesh Component is problematic at present.  Because: for dynamic meshes to work properly, the assumption is that the entire "bone hierarchy" is mirrored by entities in the entity hierarchy.
This is the case if you drag 'n' drop a mesh into the scene from the Content Browser, but it is not the case if you manually add a mesh component to an entity, and then choose a mesh from asset selection dropdown.
This commit prevents crash, but does not really solve the problem - we need a better way of handling the "bone entities"

The Hazel Tools extension wasn't able to catch unhandled exceptions thrown in C# methods called via Unmanaged to Managed Thunks, e.g `OnUpdate`, `OnPhysicsUpdate`. commits.subject: Change TransformComponent to store rotation as quaternion
commits.message:
Change TransformComponent to store rotation as quaternion

Need to store euler angles as well, see code comments for reason
This fixes:
- Import of assets where a sub-mesh is rotated around Y-axis by an exact multiple of 90 degrees
- Distortion of animated assets if bones are similarly gimbal-locked

Changes also to make manipulation of entity transforms via ImGuizmo a bit more robust.
In particular, rotating via ImGuizmo no longer forces rotation into range -180 to 180.
Activating ImGuizmo over a an entity with gimbal locked rotation is now less likely to inadvertently change the transform.
No small drift due numerical precision issues in matrix operations.

commits.subject: Fix crash at Hazelnut exit, exposed by GLFW changes
commits.message:
Fix crash at Hazelnut exit, exposed by GLFW changes

Clear out event callback before deleting layer stack.
Otherwise events raised after this point will cause a crash (Application::OnEvent() iterates the layer stack, which will be full of dangling pointers).
Clearing m_LayerStack after the delete loop is not a sufficient solution.  e.g. any one of the layer->OnDetach() could raise an event, and thus cause a call to OnEvent() (crashing on dangling pointer) _before_ we've cleared m_LayerStack.

commits.subject: Audio Events Abstraction Layer
commits.message:
Audio Events Abstraction Layer

- Redesigned the way audio playback works. Now instead of calling playback of audio sources from game's code, you post audio events. What audio events do defined in Audio Events Editor (Menubar: Edit->AudioEventsEditor).
- This is much more powerful and modern system. It allows you to hook up playback once and change which sounds are triggered to play, stop, pause (etc.) later from the Editor without having to touch code.

- Audio Events are abstract, each event can trigger playback change of multiple audio sources attached to an AudioComponent or an Audio Object requested by the client.
- E. g. an Audio Event can trigger a sequence of actions:
   - Stop audio source "X" on Object "obj_1";
   - Play audio source "Y" on Object "obj_2";

- In the future Audio Events will be able to trigger other Audio Events, changes of parameters, switches and states.

- Further into the future Audio Events will be able to trigger Audio Events of third party audio middleware like Wwise and FMOD. It will be as simple as switching an interface. All of the sound integration in game will stay the same, with no need to rewrite it for the specific middleware engine you've switched to.

- Currently we don't have Parameters, Switches, States and a way to create simple random or sequential audio source containers.
   - Parameters, Switches and States are going to be addressed in the next update of
   Audio Events Abstraction Layer.
   - Audio Source playback Containers are going to be a part of  "Playback Logic
   Design Workflow" feature set.

commits.subject: Updated PhysX to 4.1.2 + other changes
commits.message:
Updated PhysX to 4.1.2 + other changes

- Now using release build of PhysX in release, instead of checked (we may want to consider using checked for release mode and release version for dist mode)
- Mesh Collider assets are now aware of what type of collider they're using
- No longer identify collider type by mesh type.. That's not a good way of handling mesh colliders.
- Mesh & StaticMesh now support both triangle AND convex mesh colliders
- Better validation for physics shapes
- Fixed bug with deserializing MeshColliderComponents
**NOTE:** We will soon introduce the concept of complex and simple mesh colliders! We'll almost always generate both a triangle mesh collider, and a convex mesh collider, that will (by default) be used for different parts of the simulation. It will be a lot more similar to Unreals way of handling mesh colliders, rather than Unitys (Unreals way of handling it is far better anyway)

- Auto-save also the AudioCommandRegistry
- (shouldn't be any need to auto-save the AssetRegistry since that is saved to disk whenever its changed anyway)
- git ignore files with ".auto" extension as there is no need to version control these auto-saved backups

commits.subject: Improvements to scene entity lookup
commits.message:
Improvements to scene entity lookup

- Remove Scene::FindEntityByUUID, and replace with two functions as follows:
     Scene::GetEntityWithUUID - returns entity with specified id.  entity must exist otherwise runtime error
     Scene::TryGetEntityWithUUID - returns entity with specified id, or empty entity if doesn't exist - caller must check returned entity before use
- Implementation of the two GetEntityWithUUID functions uses internal entity id map (as opposed to searching through view<IDComponent>)
- Scene entity id map is now private to the scene.  External users of Scene objects should use GetEntityWithUUID or TryGetEntityWithUUID, depending on use-case
- Remove unnecessary function Entity::HasParent():  if(entity.GetParent()) {...} achieves the same thing
   This also avoids looking up the entity ids twice, since code like if(HasParent()) { GetParent() ...} is removed.
- Remove double-lookup of the entity id in Entity::GetParent()
- hashing a UUID now returns the UUID value directly

commits.subject: Make entities with rigged meshes work (mostly) with duplication and prefabs
commits.message:
Make entities with rigged meshes work (mostly) with duplication and prefabs

- Duplicating an entity with child rigged mesh components will now work *provided that* you duplicate the whole thing (i.e. the entity that you duplicate must be the top level "parent" that contains both the rigged mesh entities, and all the bone transform entities (in other words, its the "root" entity from the original mesh asset)

- Fixed a bug where if there were multiple entities with same rigged mesh in the scene, then they could not be selected properly.
  This was due to some confusion between indexes and offsets.  Renamed some variables called "offset" to "index" to avoid this in future.
  An index is something like 0, 1, 2, ... generally used to index into an array.
  An offset (at least in the context of vulkan) is generally used to mean a number of byte offset into a buffer.

commits.subject: WIP: Make Animation Go Again
commits.message:
WIP: Make Animation Go Again

With the new mesh system, when a rigged mesh is imported, "bones" from the rig end up as entities in the scene hierarchy.  Those bone entities contain just one component: namely a transform.
This commit:
- Ties those transforms back to the mesh skinning.  If you change the transform of the "arm" component, say, then the mesh's arm will move accordingly.
- Resolves a long standing issue where entities that share the same animated mesh could not be animated independently.  Now, they can be.  Sharing animated meshes also works correctly with the instanced rendering (i.e. they will be instanced).
- Add a 2nd stormtrooper into the AnimationTest scene to demonstrate previous item.
- Add a light sabre as a child entity of the "right hand" of player stormtrooper mesh.  This demonstrates how carried items can be automatically moved by the bone transforms of an animated entity.

Still to do:
- prefabs with rigged meshes not working
- duplicating entities with rigged meshes not working
- applying animation assets to the "bone entities" not yet implemented  (with this commit, you can only "animate" meshes by manually changing the transforms of the bone entities in the scene properties panel)
- performance (current implementation is known to be relatively slow. This will be addressed once its all working)

commits.subject: FBX asset workflow - fix scaling issues  (SCENE BREAKING CHANGE)
commits.message:
FBX asset workflow - fix scaling issues  (SCENE BREAKING CHANGE)

- Use assimp "aiProcess_GlobalScale" post processing step to scale assets where native units are cm (such as fbx)
  This is not a big deal for non-animated assets, but it is important for rigged meshes (e.g. like on animation branch)
  Committing this to master because it is a scene-breaking change, so good to get it in sooner rather than later.

- Removed not-used Pilot_LP_Animated asset

- Fixed all broken scenes by re-exporting all fbx assets, removing any scaling hacks.
  For Blender, the fbx workflow is now:
  - Scene unit system set to "metric", with scale = 1.0
  - Scale your model until the dimensions are what you want.  1m in Blender will be 1 unit in Hazel
  - When exporting as fbx, set the transform scale to 1.0,  and under "Apply Scalings", select "FBX Units Scale"

If you are using fbx assets in scenes external to the Hazel repo, you will need to re-export those assets per workflow above.
(otherwise they will all come out 100x too large in Hazel)

commits.subject: Greatly improved animation root motion
commits.message:
Greatly improved animation root motion

- Root motion works with animations from Mixamo directly.  Mixamo animations typically have the hip as root bone, rather than a "proper" root bone at the model origin.
The hip has motion in it (e.g. jiggly rotations) other than what you actually want as the "root motion" for your character.
It doesn't matter it all works.  There is no need to pre-process Mixamo animations in Blender (or other tool) to try and add "proper" root bones (but you can do that if you want to, Hazel will work with that too)

- Added a "Root Motion Target" so that you can control which entity root motion is applied to (e.g. for situation where the main "player" entity is actually a parent of the entity that is controlling the animation)

- Added some "debugging" aids added to Animation Component in editor (you can pause/play the animation, step it forwards/backwards)

commits.subject: Fix crash at Hazelnut exit, exposed by GLFW changes
commits.message:
Fix crash at Hazelnut exit, exposed by GLFW changes

Clear out event callback before deleting layer stack.
Otherwise events raised after this point will cause a crash (Application::OnEvent() iterates the layer stack, which will be full of dangling pointers).
Clearing m_LayerStack after the delete loop is not a sufficient solution.  e.g. any one of the layer->OnDetach() could raise an event, and thus cause a call to OnEvent() (crashing on dangling pointer) _before_ we've cleared m_LayerStack.

commits.subject: Add control of "root motion" in animations
commits.message:
Add control of "root motion" in animations

- Can specify one of the following options to handle motion of the root bone of an animated mesh:
  * default:  don't do anything special.
  * in-place:  movement of root bone is stripped from the animation, making it play "in-place".  Useful if you wish to move the characters around "manually" via game logic.
  * apply:  movement of root bone is stripped (as per in-place), and that movement is returned from AnimationController::OnUpdate() so that caller can, for example, apply that motion to the character transform.

Note: The only root motion we deal with is translation in the forward (Z-axis) direction.  Translations in other axes, rotations, and scales, are still applied to the root bone regardless of "root motion" setting.
(this might need to change, later,  (e.g. a "climbing" animation might wish to return y-axis translation as the "root motion"))

commits.subject: WIP: animation
commits.message:
WIP: animation

- Add Animation (a single animation "clip"), and AnimationController (aka. state machine) assets.
- Add "serializers" for Animation and AnimationController assets.  Animation comes from digital content files (such as fbx).  AnimationController comes from Hazel .hanim files.
  The way this is intended to work is that there will be a rigged mesh in one DCC file, like "character model.fbx"
  Then animation clips will be in separate DCC files, like "idle.fbx", "walk.fbx", "jump.fbx", and so on.  Later we could consider supporting multiple clips in one file.
  The AnimationController then references these Animation assets.  Each Animation asset is one "state" that the AnimationController's state machine can be in.
- Move animation stuff out of Mesh and into Animation/AnimationController etc.
- Add AnimationComponent, which references an AnimationController asset.
- Update SceneHierarcyPanel etc. etc. to handle new AnimationComponent.
- Add reminder comments to top of Component.h for what needs to be done when a new type of component is added

Notes:
- AnimationController is mostly just a placeholder at present.  It supports one animation clip only, and the state is either playing, or paused.  That's it.
- The code needs to be re-structured to deal with mesh and/or animation assets shared between multiple entities.  Currently you cannot, for example, have two (animated) enemies in the scene that share the same mesh and animation assets.

commits.subject: Added custom icons for Point Light and Sound Source
commits.message:
Added custom icons for Point Light and Sound Source

Included template file icons.psd.

To create new icons:
----------------------
1. Duplicate artboard.
2. Make your shape inside of "SHAPE STYLING" folder.
3. Create a SHADE shape which should compliment and/or match some geometric feature of your main shape, and somewhat indicate volume/depth.
4. Make your SHADE shape clipping to the "CLIP SHADE TO" folder.

5) You can check how your icon looks with tint by enabling and changing Color Overlay effect on the "SHAPE STYLING" folder.

Tinting can be used in engine to indicate activation state (for example).

commits.subject: Added Low-Pass and High-Pass filters. Reverb setup now takes into account sample rate.
commits.message:
Added Low-Pass and High-Pass filters. Reverb setup now takes into account sample rate.

Low-Pass and High-Pass filters are not hooked up to the ScriptEngine, it would require writing code that's going to be replaced by a bigger system within Audio Events Abstraction Layer.
So for now you can just set the filter values for each new sound voice.

Values for the LPF and HPF are a bit finicky, the most useful range is at the very beginning < 0.1, which corresponds to < 2kHz - it's basically linear. Because math is hard.
